name: Plugins CI

# The whole pull request check set behind one caller, so a plugin's own workflow carries its name
# and nothing else, and a check added here reaches every plugin without a pull request against any
# of them. Codex review is deliberately not part of this -- see the note at the bottom of the file.
#
# Checks are opt *out*. A new check added here runs everywhere by default, which is the point; an
# opt-in switch would leave a new check running nowhere until every caller adds a line.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plugin-name:
        description: "Name of the plugin, e.g. LoginLdap"
        required: true
        type: string

      # --- opt-outs ---
      skip-phpcs:
        description: "Do not run the PHPCS check"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-phpstan:
        description: "Do not run the PHPStan analysis"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-license-check:
        description: "Do not run the license check"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-ai-checklist:
        description: "Do not run the AI checklist gate"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-min-php-lint:
        description: "Do not run the minimum PHP lint over scoped dependencies"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-compatibility:
        description: "Do not compile the plugin's stylesheets and templates against its minimum and maximum Matomo"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-timezone-safety:
        description: "Do not run the timezone safety static scan or its regression coverage check"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip-release-date:
        description: "Do not run the release date check, which only fails a plugin that calls plugin-dev-release.yml"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

      # --- pass-through, named per check because four of them take a php-version ---
      phpcs-php-version:
        description: "PHP version for the PHPCS run. PHPCS needs at least 7.4, so matomo5_min_php is too low."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo6_min_php'
      phpstan-php-version:
        description: "PHP version for the PHPStan runs"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo6_min_php'
      compatibility-php-version:
        description: "PHP version for the compatibility runs, used by any matomo-targets entry that sets no php of its own"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo6_min_php'
      dependent-plugins:
        description: "Space-separated repository slugs PHPStan and the compatibility check need checked out, e.g. 'innocraft/plugin-Funnels'"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      matomo-targets:
        description: "JSON array of {target, php} objects, one PHPStan run and one compatibility run each"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '[{"target": "minimum_required_matomo"}, {"target": "maximum_supported_matomo"}]'
      verify-hook:
        description: "Run the hook-check job, failing when the plugin ships a .git-hooks-matomo/pre-push that differs from the canonical copy. Only for repositories that still ship their own; prefer pointing core.hooksPath at this repository instead."
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      fail-on-missing-header:
        description: "Treat source files without any recognized license header as license-check errors"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      min-php-lint-path:
        description: "Directory the minimum PHP lint parses. Skipped when absent, so a plugin with no scoped dependencies needs no opt-out."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'vendor/prefixed'
      min-php-lint-php-version:
        description: "Override the floor the minimum PHP lint derives from the plugin's composer.json and plugin.json. Accepts a major.minor version such as 8.1, or one of the shared aliases. Leave unset unless the declared floor is wrong."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      timezone-regression-exempt:
        description: "Why this plugin needs no timezone regression suite although the timezone check found date or site-timezone logic. Empty means it is not exempt."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

      # --- refs ---
      scripts-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/github-action-tests for the shared helper scripts and the composite action the compatibility check runs"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of this repository for the timezone checker, pre-push hook, PHPStan bootstrap, caller concurrency guard, plugin floor resolver, compatibility test generator and release date check"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      script-ref:
        description: "Ref of this repository for the license check script"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'

    secrets:
      TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        [REDACTED] "Needed only when dependent-plugins names a private repository"
        required: false

# The union of what the checks below need, which is the cost of one caller: a plugin that only
# wanted PHPCS previously needed no scopes at all, and now grants the checklist gate's three.
permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

# One lane. This was briefly two -- a `-code` lane and an `-edited` one -- because a description
# edit re-ran the workflow while skipping every check below, so letting it supersede a push's run
# cancelled the analysis and replaced it with nothing (UsersFlow#135). Splitting the lanes stopped
# the cancellation but not the damage: a run whose checks are all skipped concludes `success`, and
# GitHub resolves a commit's overall verdict from the newest check suite per workflow, by suite
# CREATION time. So the edited run's green suite replaced the code run's verdict wholesale --
# measured on a probe: the pull request read "All checks have passed" 16 seconds after the edit,
# while the analysis was still running, and stayed green when it failed two minutes later. Nine of
# the fleet's migration pull requests had a red license check hidden that way.
#
# The fix is to stop skipping (see the jobs below), which removes the reason for two lanes: every
# run does the whole check set, so any run superseding another is telling the truth. The cost is
# one extra run of these checks per description edit. The compatibility job is most of that: it
# installs Matomo against MySQL once per matomo-targets entry and runs PHPUnit. The full test
# matrix lives in matomo-tests.yml, which does not subscribe to `edited`, so it is untouched.
#
# Static prefix, for the same reason plugin-codex-review.yml uses one: in a reusable workflow
# ${{ github.workflow }} resolves to the CALLER's workflow name, so a group built from it collides
# with a caller group of the same name and GitHub kills the run with "a deadlock was detected for
# concurrency group ...". Callers declare no concurrency of their own -- which the caller-concurrency
# job below asserts, because a caller-level group silently defeats all of this: a called workflow
# cannot override it, and the group never matches this static prefix, so GitHub raises no deadlock
# error to say so.
concurrency:
  group: plugin-ci-shared-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# The caller subscribes to `edited` so the checklist gate re-runs when a description is fixed, and
# every job below runs on that event like any other. No job may condition itself on
# github.event.action, and tests/plugin_ci_invariants_test.sh fails the build if one does: the
# moment a job runs in some runs of a commit and not others, that commit has two runs disagreeing
# about what was checked, and the newer one wins whether or not it checked anything.
#
# Skipping on an input (skip-phpcs, verify-hook) is fine and is not the same thing -- an input is
# fixed for the commit, so every run of it makes the same decision and no run can contradict
# another.
jobs:
  # It used to carry a concurrency lane of its own, to span the two workflow-level lanes and stop a
  # stale checklist verdict landing last. With one lane that is what the workflow-level group
  # already does, and a second group here would only add a way for the two to disagree.
  ai-checklist:
    # pull_request only, because the gate reads the pull request's description and there is none on
    # a push or a dispatch. Callers subscribe to those so one badge on this workflow can report the
    # default branch, and without this the gate would fail every such run. Conditioning on the
    # event NAME is narrower than conditioning on the event ACTION, which every run of a pull
    # request carries, but it is not unconditionally safe: a caller subscribing to both
    # `pull_request` and `push: branches: ['**.x-dev']` puts two runs on one commit when the pull
    # request's own head branch matches that filter -- a forward-merge from 5.x-dev, say -- and the
    # push run skips this gate. Measured on a probe, twice: GitHub created the `pull_request` run
    # three to four seconds AFTER the `push` run, on the pull request being opened and on a later
    # push to it, so the failing suite was the newest and the verdict held. That ordering is not
    # documented and the margin is seconds, so this is recorded rather than relied on.
    # The release date pull request plugin-dev-release.yml opens is passed inside the called
    # workflow, not skipped here: a skip here reports as `ai-checklist`, never as the gate's own
    # check, so a branch requiring the gate would hold that pull request forever.
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-ai-checklist && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-ai-checklist.yml@main
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

  # The lane above is worth nothing if the caller declares a group of its own: this workflow cannot
  # override it, and its name never matches the static prefix above, so GitHub raises no deadlock
  # error either. Nothing on the pull request would say why the analysis vanished, which is why the
  # caller's side of the contract is checked rather than only written in the README.
  #
  # No skip- input, unlike every check here: the way out is to delete the offending block, so a
  # caller never needs the guard turned off, and a switch for it is the hole it exists to close.
  caller-concurrency:
    name: Caller concurrency
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # It parses YAML that a contributor controls, and safe_load stops object construction but not
    # alias expansion, so a YAML bomb would otherwise sit on the six-hour default.
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      # Unique so it cannot collide with a directory the caller tracks.
      WORKFLOWS_DIR: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The workflow definitions and nothing else: this reads the caller's configuration and
          # never its code. On a `pull_request` the checked-out merge ref carries the version of
          # the workflow that actually ran, which is the copy whose group governed this run.
          sparse-checkout: .github/workflows
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # The guard parses the caller's YAML and fails closed without PyYAML, so install it rather
      # than trust the runner image to keep shipping it. `apt-get update` first, and only when the
      # import fails: the runner image ships no package index, so a bare `apt-get install` can
      # only ever report the package already present -- which is exactly what it does today, and
      # it would fail to locate anything on the day the image stops shipping it.
      - name: Install the YAML parser the guard needs
        run: python3 -P -c 'import yaml' || { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-yaml; }

      - name: Check the caller declares no concurrency of its own
        run: bash "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_caller_concurrency.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF" .

  # A called workflow, like every check here, and that is what keeps its skip honest: an inline
  # job publishes its check run under one name whether it ran or was skipped, so an `edited`
  # run's `skipped` lands on top of the code run's verdict. Write any new check the same way --
  # tests/plugin_ci_invariants_test.sh has the full reasoning and enforces it.
  #
  # Its own check rather than a step inside PHPStan, where it used to live. A vendored hook
  # drifting is not a finding about the plugin's code, and running the comparison before the
  # analysis meant a drifted hook both reported as red PHPStan and suppressed the analysis that
  # would have said something real. Opt in through verify-hook, so there is no skip- input: a
  # plugin turns it off by not turning it on.
  hook-check:
    if: ${{ inputs.verify-hook }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-hook-check.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      workflows-ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}

  phpcs:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-phpcs }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-phpcs.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      plugin-name: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
      php-version: ${{ inputs.phpcs-php-version }}
      scripts-ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}

  phpstan:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-phpstan }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-phpstan.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      plugin-name: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
      dependent-plugins: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins }}
      php-version: ${{ inputs.phpstan-php-version }}
      matomo-targets: ${{ inputs.matomo-targets }}
      scripts-ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
      workflows-ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
    secrets:
      TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

  compatibility:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-compatibility }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-compatibility.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      plugin-name: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
      dependent-plugins: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins }}
      php-version: ${{ inputs.compatibility-php-version }}
      matomo-targets: ${{ inputs.matomo-targets }}
      scripts-ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
      workflows-ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
    secrets:
      TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

  # Its own job rather than a step inside another. Folding a second check into an existing one
  # is what made hook drift surface as a red PHPStan check that had analysed nothing, and #12
  # has only just unpicked that. The cost is a job that starts and finds nothing to do in the
  # plugins with no scoped dependencies, which is seconds and no PHP setup.
  min-php-lint:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-min-php-lint }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-min-php-lint.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      lint-path: ${{ inputs.min-php-lint-path }}
      php-version: ${{ inputs.min-php-lint-php-version }}
      scripts-ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
      workflows-ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}

  license-check:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-license-check }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-license-check.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      fail-on-missing-header: ${{ inputs.fail-on-missing-header }}
      script-ref: ${{ inputs.script-ref }}

  timezone-safety:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-timezone-safety }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-timezone-safety.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      plugin-name: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
      workflows-ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
      timezone-regression-exempt: ${{ inputs.timezone-regression-exempt }}

  # Passes in a plugin that does not call plugin-dev-release.yml, so a plugin opts in by adopting
  # the weekly release and the check needs no input of its own.
  release-date:
    if: ${{ !inputs.skip-release-date }}
    uses: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-release-date-check.yml@main
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      workflows-ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}

# Codex review is not called from here, and should not be. It runs on `pull_request_target` with
# secrets available, gated on a label; every check above runs on `pull_request`. Putting both in
# one caller means one workflow file declaring both events, and the code checks then need an
# `if:` excluding pull_request_target or they execute pull request code in a context that can
# read secrets. A single missing condition there is a credential leak, not a red build.
#
# Its own `automation-paths` guard also names .github/workflows/codex-review.yml as a file that
# must get human review before a review runs, so moving it into a differently named wrapper
# removes that control.
#
# Its wrapper is a stable file that rarely changes; the logic it calls lives here, so the
# per-plugin cost is paid once rather than on every change to how the review works.

name: Tests

on: pull_request

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  license-check-script:
    name: License check script tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run tests
        run: bash tests/license_check_test.sh

  pre-push-hook:
    name: Pre-push hook tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # The fixtures drive hooks/pre-push against throwaway repositories with a stub analyser, so
      # the job needs neither PHP nor a Matomo checkout.
      - name: Run tests
        run: bash tests/pre_push_base_branch_test.sh

  plugin-release-scripts:
    name: Plugin release script tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install the YAML parser the release date check needs
        run: python3 -c 'import yaml' || { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-yaml; }
      - name: Check changelog dating
        run: bash tests/update_changelog_date_test.sh
      - name: Check release preparation, dating, tagging and the release date check
        run: bash tests/plugin_dev_release_test.sh
      - name: Check merging the release date pull request
        run: bash tests/merge_plugin_release_date_pr_test.sh
      - name: Check GitHub release publishing
        run: bash tests/publish_plugin_release_test.sh

  plugin-ci-invariants:
    name: Plugins CI invariants
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # Same reasoning as codex-review-invariants below: the script parses the workflow with
      # PyYAML and fails closed without it, so install it rather than trust the runner image.
      - name: Install the YAML parser the invariants need
        run: python3 -c 'import yaml' || { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-yaml; }

      - name: Run tests
        run: bash tests/plugin_ci_invariants_test.sh

      - name: Check the timezone safety workflow contract
        run: bash tests/timezone_workflow_invariants_test.sh

      - name: Check the timezone safety workflow runtime
        run: bash tests/timezone_workflow_runtime_test.sh

      - name: Check the timezone safety script
        run: bash tests/timezone_safety_test.sh

      - name: Check the timezone regression coverage script
        run: bash tests/timezone_regression_coverage_test.sh

      - name: Check the timezone regression coverage step
        run: bash tests/timezone_coverage_step_test.sh

      # Runs in this job rather than one of its own so it lands inside a check `main` already
      # requires, and because it asserts the other half of the same contract: the umbrella owning
      # the concurrency group here, and the caller declaring none that would replace it.
      - name: Check the caller concurrency guard
        run: bash tests/caller_concurrency_test.sh

      - name: Check the development release workflow invariants
        run: bash tests/plugin_dev_release_invariants_test.sh

      - name: Check the pre-push hook sync check
        run: bash tests/hook_sync_test.sh

      # Same reasoning as the two above: it lands inside a check `main` already requires. It also
      # needs PyYAML, which this job has already installed, to read the sweep's shell out of the
      # workflow rather than slicing the file by indentation.
      - name: Check the branch sweep
        run: bash tests/branch_sweep_test.sh

      - name: Check the branch sweep's inactivity check
        run: bash tests/inactivity_check_test.sh

      - name: Check the minimum PHP lint
        run: bash tests/min_php_lint_test.sh

      - name: Check the vendored dependencies update
        run: bash tests/vendored_deps_update_test.sh

      # Last, because it swaps the runner's PHP for the oldest any matomo-targets entry can select,
      # so that php -l in the test checks the generated files against the real floor.
      - uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: '7.2'

      - name: Check the compatibility test generator
        run: bash tests/compatibility_checks_test.sh

  codex-review-invariants:
    name: Codex review invariants
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # The invariants parse the workflow with PyYAML. It happens to be present on
      # ubuntu-24.04 today, but a check that guards security controls should not depend on
      # what a runner image ships: it fails closed without it, and a job that reliably
      # fails is no better than one that silently skips.
      # apt, not pip: `pip install` into system Python on ubuntu-24.04 can refuse with PEP 668
      # externally-managed-environment, and the distro package is a pinned, signed artifact.
      # `apt-get update` first, and only when the import fails: the image ships no package index,
      # so a bare `apt-get install` can only report what is already present -- which is what it
      # does today, and it would locate nothing on the day the image stops shipping it.
      - name: Install the YAML parser the invariants need
        run: python3 -c 'import yaml' || { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-yaml; }

      # The review's other half lives in a private repository whose tests cannot see
      # this workflow, so the controls that live here are asserted here.
      - name: Check the Codex review workflow's security invariants
        run: bash tests/codex_review_invariants_test.sh

  actionlint:
    name: Workflow lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # Parsing the YAML only proves it is YAML. actionlint checks the Actions
      # schema and expression syntax, and shellcheck runs over every `run:` block.
      - name: Run actionlint
        env:
          ACTIONLINT_VERSION: 1.7.12
          # sha256 of actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz, from the release's
          # checksums.txt. Bump both together when moving version.
          ACTIONLINT_SHA256: 8aca8db96f1b94770f1b0d72b6dddcb1ebb8123cb3712530b08cc387b349a3d8
        run: |
          ARCHIVE="actionlint_${ACTIONLINT_VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
          curl -fsSL -o "$ARCHIVE" \
            "https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/v${ACTIONLINT_VERSION}/${ARCHIVE}"
          echo "${ACTIONLINT_SHA256}  ${ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum --check --strict
          tar xz -f "$ARCHIVE" actionlint
          # ubuntu-24.04 ships shellcheck, so actionlint lints every `run:` block too.
          ./actionlint -color

      # actionlint only reaches shell inside workflows. The hook ships to every plugin
      # repository and the scripts run in their CI, so lint them directly as well.
      - name: Run shellcheck over the standalone scripts
        run: shellcheck --severity=style hooks/pre-push scripts/bash/*.sh tests/*.sh

      # actionlint checks that a pin is *shaped* like a SHA, not that the commit exists. One pin
      # in this stack named no commit at all and still linted clean. The Codex review cannot catch
      # it either -- it runs read-only with no network by design -- so it is checked here, in
      # ordinary pull request CI where a token is available and no privileged trigger is involved.
      # bootstrap-phpstan.php is copied into a Matomo root and executed on every pre-5.4.0
      # PHPStan leg, so a syntax error there breaks the analysis rather than this repository.
      - name: Lint the shipped PHP
        run: php -l artifacts/bootstrap-phpstan.php

      - name: Check every pinned action resolves
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: bash scripts/bash/check_action_pins.sh

<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;

return static function (RectorConfig $rectorConfig): void {
    $targetPhpVersion = getenv('RECTOR_DOWNGRADE_PHP_VERSION') ?: '7.3';

    $supportedTargets = [
        '7.3' => \Rector\Set\ValueObject\DowngradeLevelSetList::DOWN_TO_PHP_73,
        '8.1' => \Rector\Set\ValueObject\DowngradeLevelSetList::DOWN_TO_PHP_81,
    ];

    if (!isset($supportedTargets[$targetPhpVersion])) {
        throw new \InvalidArgumentException(sprintf(
            'Unsupported Rector downgrade PHP version "%s". Supported values: %s',
            $targetPhpVersion,
            implode(', ', array_keys($supportedTargets))
        ));
    }

    $rectorConfig->sets([
        $supportedTargets[$targetPhpVersion],
    ]);

    // Both exceptions below are PHP 8.0 downgrade rules, which are only registered when the target is
    // below 8.0. Listing them for a higher target makes Rector warn that they are never registered.
    if (version_compare($targetPhpVersion, '8.0', '<')) {
        $rectorConfig->skip([
            // Attributes are kept rather than downgraded: PHP 7 treats `#[` as a comment, so they are inert there while
            // still applying on PHP 8. That only holds while each attribute sits on its own line, which the plugins that
            // support PHP 7 arrange via a patcher in their scoper.inc.php.
            \Rector\DowngradePhp80\Rector\Class_\DowngradeAttributeToAnnotationRector::class,
            // Skip downgrading Token for php-parser since it already provides a polyfill
            \Rector\DowngradePhp80\Rector\StaticCall\DowngradePhpTokenRector::class => [
                '*/vendor/prefixed/nikic/php-parser/*',
            ],
        ]);
    }
};

# Scopes a plugin's installed dependencies into vendor/prefixed, transpiles them down to the PHP the
# plugin supports, and checks the result.
#
# The work is scripts/bash/scope_plugin_dependencies.sh, which developers run locally to rebuild the
# same tree. Run composer install or composer update in the plugin first; the scoper prefixes
# whatever the unprefixed vendor/ tree holds.
#
# Needs php 8.1 or later, composer, jq, git and curl on PATH, and python3 for downgrade-php auto below Matomo 6. It sets up no PHP of its own, so it never changes the PHP
# that later steps of the caller's job run on.

name: Scope plugin dependencies
description: Scopes a plugin's dependencies with matomo-scoper, downgrades them with Rector, and checks the scoped tree.

inputs:
  plugin-path:
    description: "Path to the plugin checkout. It must be a git checkout, because the tree check compares against HEAD."
    required: false
    default: '.'
  downgrade-php:
    description: "PHP version to transpile vendor/prefixed down to: 'auto' reads it from the plugin (8.1 when it requires Matomo 6 or later, or PHP 8.1 or later, 7.3 otherwise), 'none' skips Rector, or pass 7.3 or 8.1."
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  allowed-unprefixed-namespaces:
    description: "Whitespace-separated namespaces allowed to remain outside Matomo\\Dependencies\\<plugin> in vendor/prefixed, besides Composer\\Autoload, which is always allowed."
    required: false
    default: ''
  scoper-ref:
    description: "Ref of matomo-org/matomo-scoper. Empty uses the commit scripts/bash/scope_plugin_dependencies.sh pins."
    required: false
    default: ''

outputs:
  plugin-name:
    description: "The plugin's name, read from plugin.json."
    value: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.plugin-name }}
  downgrade-php-version:
    description: "The PHP version vendor/prefixed was transpiled to, or empty when Rector was skipped."
    value: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.downgrade }}
  enum-list:
    description: "A file listing the enums vendor/prefixed declared before Rector ran, one per line."
    value: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.enum-list }}

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Scope, downgrade and check
      id: scope
      shell: bash
      env:
        PLUGIN_PATH: ${{ inputs.plugin-path }}
        DOWNGRADE_INPUT: ${{ inputs.downgrade-php }}
        ALLOWED: ${{ inputs.allowed-unprefixed-namespaces }}
        SCOPER_REF: ${{ inputs.scoper-ref }}
        # In the runner's temp directory rather than the workspace, where the caller's plugin
        # checkout, and whatever else it globs, also lives.
        TOOLS: ${{ runner.temp }}/scope-dependencies
      run: |
        args=(--downgrade-php="$DOWNGRADE_INPUT" --scoper-ref="$SCOPER_REF" --tools-dir="$TOOLS" --enum-list="$TOOLS/enums.txt")
        for namespace in $ALLOWED; do
          args+=(--allow-namespace="$namespace")
        done
        bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/../../scripts/bash/scope_plugin_dependencies.sh" "${args[@]}" "$PLUGIN_PATH"
        echo "enum-list=$TOOLS/enums.txt" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#!/bin/bash
# Invariants for .github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml, the umbrella every plugin calls.
# Usage: bash tests/plugin_ci_invariants_test.sh
#
# The property these protect: every run of this workflow on a commit checks the same things, so no
# run can supersede another while having checked less.
#
# It is worth stating why, because the obvious shortcut breaks it. The umbrella subscribes to the
# `edited` pull request action so the checklist gate re-runs when a description is fixed, and it is
# tempting to skip the code checks on that action since an edit changes no file. But a run whose
# checks are all skipped concludes `success`, and GitHub resolves a commit's verdict from the
# newest check suite per workflow, ordered by suite CREATION time -- so the edited run's green
# suite replaces the code run's verdict, even while the code run is still going, and even when it
# later fails. Measured on a probe; nine of the fleet's migration pull requests had a red license
# check hidden that way.
#
# Hence: no job may condition itself on github.event.action. Conditioning on an INPUT is fine, and
# is not the same thing -- an input is fixed for the commit, so every run makes the same decision.
# The second rule, that a job carrying any `if:` must be a called workflow, covers the remaining
# legitimate skips: a called workflow's skip reports as `<caller job>` while a real run reports as
# `<caller job>/<job name>`, so the two can never collide by name.
set -u

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
WORKFLOW="$ROOT/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml"

# Jobs that are not plugin checks and so carry no skip- input. The concurrency guard asserts the
# caller's half of a contract it can always satisfy by deleting a block, so it never needs a way
# out, and a switch to turn it off is the hole it exists to close.
export GUARD_JOBS="caller-concurrency"

# Jobs a caller has to ask for, and the input each one asks through. An opt-in check already has
# an off switch -- not asking -- so a skip- input beside it would be a second way to say the same
# thing, and the opt-out default that skip- exists to protect does not apply to a check that runs
# nowhere by default. The input is named here because the assertions below pin its polarity and its
# default, not merely that the job consults something.
export OPT_IN_JOBS="hook-check:verify-hook"

# The hook check's one home. Gutting the job's step would leave `verify-hook: true` silently
# checking nothing, which is worse than the misplacement this replaced.
export HOOK_SCRIPT="check_hook_sync.sh"

# Jobs that cannot run outside a pull request. Callers subscribe to push and workflow_dispatch so
# that one badge on their workflow reports the default branch, and the checklist gate reads a
# description that only a pull request has -- so losing this condition fails every push run, on
# the very badge the triggers exist to make trustworthy.
export PULL_REQUEST_ONLY_JOBS="ai-checklist"

# The invariants parse YAML with PyYAML. It happens to be present on ubuntu-24.04 today, but a
# check that guards a fleet-wide workflow should not depend on what a runner image ships: it
# fails closed without it, and a job that reliably fails is no better than one that silently skips.
if ! python3 -c 'import yaml' 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "FAIL - PyYAML is not available, so these invariants cannot be checked"
  exit 1
fi

python3 - "$WORKFLOW" <<'PY'
import os, re, sys, yaml

workflow_path = sys.argv[1]
guard_jobs = set(os.environ['GUARD_JOBS'].split())
opt_in_jobs = dict(pair.split(':') for pair in os.environ['OPT_IN_JOBS'].split())
hook_script = os.environ['HOOK_SCRIPT']
pull_request_only = set(os.environ['PULL_REQUEST_ONLY_JOBS'].split())

with open(workflow_path) as handle:
    doc = yaml.safe_load(handle)

# PyYAML resolves the bare `on:` key to the boolean True.
triggers = doc.get('on', doc.get(True)) or {}
jobs = doc.get('jobs') or {}

tests = 0
failures = []


def check(description, condition):
    global tests
    tests += 1
    if condition:
        print(f"ok - {description}")
    else:
        print(f"FAIL - {description}")
        failures.append(description)


def conditions_on_event_action(job):
    """Rule one: does this job run in some runs of a commit and not others?"""
    return 'github.event.action' in ''.join(str((job or {}).get('if', '')).split())


def can_be_skipped(job):
    """Rule two's trigger. `needs:` counts -- a job whose dependency is skipped is skipped too."""
    job = job or {}
    return bool(job.get('if')) or bool(job.get('needs'))


def called_workflow_file(job):
    """The workflow in this repository that a job calls, or '' when it calls none."""
    uses = str((job or {}).get('uses', ''))
    if 'plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/' not in uses:
        return ''
    return uses.split('@')[0].split('/.github/workflows/')[-1]


check("the umbrella is a reusable workflow", 'workflow_call' in triggers)
check("it declares at least one job", bool(jobs))

# One lane. Splitting it by event action was the previous answer to an edited run cancelling the
# analysis, and it traded that for the worse failure described at the top of this file. With every
# run doing the whole check set, a run that supersedes another is telling the truth.
concurrency = doc.get('concurrency') or {}
# Whitespace-insensitive, so the assertions pin the expression's meaning and not one spelling of it.
group = str(concurrency.get('group', ''))
group_squashed = ''.join(group.split())
check("the umbrella declares a concurrency group", bool(group))
check(
    "the concurrency group does not split runs by event action",
    'github.event.action' not in group_squashed,
)
# github.workflow resolves to the caller's workflow name here, so a group built from it matches a
# caller's own group and GitHub kills the run for a concurrency deadlock rather than running it.
check(
    "the concurrency group uses a static prefix, not github.workflow",
    'github.workflow' not in group_squashed,
)
# Losing the per-pull-request scope is the worst regression available here: every open pull request
# in the repository would share one lane and cancel each other's checks.
check(
    "the concurrency group is scoped per pull request",
    'github.event.pull_request.number' in group_squashed,
)
# Without this the group queues instead of superseding, so the file still reads as intended while
# doing the opposite -- a stale run finishes last and its verdict is the one that sticks.
check(
    "the concurrency group supersedes rather than queues",
    concurrency.get('cancel-in-progress') is True,
)

# The lane above is defeated by a caller declaring a group of its own, silently: a called workflow
# cannot override it, and the name never matches the static prefix, so no deadlock error is raised.
# Deleting the job that catches that would restore the silence.
for name in sorted(guard_jobs):
    steps = (jobs.get(name) or {}).get('steps') or []
    runs_guard = any(
        'check_caller_concurrency.sh' in str(step.get('run', ''))
        for step in steps
        if isinstance(step, dict)
    )
    check(f"{name} runs the caller concurrency guard", runs_guard)

# The two rules that keep every run of a commit equivalent. See the top of this file for why.
for name, job in jobs.items():
    condition = str(job.get('if', ''))

    # Rule one. A job conditioned on the event action runs in some runs of a commit and not
    # others, and the run that skipped it still concludes and still supersedes.
    check(
        f"{name} does not condition itself on the event action",
        not conditions_on_event_action(job),
    )

    # Rule two. A job that can be skipped at all -- on an input, or on the event name -- has to be
    # a called workflow. A skipped job still publishes a check run, and one defined in this file
    # publishes it under the same name whether it ran or was skipped, so the skip lands on top of
    # whatever an earlier run concluded and a skipped required check counts as a passing one. A
    # called workflow cannot: its skip reports as `<caller job>` and a real run as
    # `<caller job>/<job name>`. Seen on plugin-LogViewer b0506a2b, where `ci / Hook check` went
    # success and then skipped on one commit while `ci / phpcs / PHPCS` came through untouched.
    #
    # `needs:` counts too: a job whose dependency is skipped is skipped with it, and inline it
    # publishes that skip under the name it uses when it runs. No job here declares one today, so
    # this is a guard on the shape rather than on the current file.
    #
    # Exempt only on being unskippable, which is what actually makes an inline job safe.
    if can_be_skipped(job):
        check(
            f"{name} is a called workflow, so skipping it cannot overwrite a real verdict",
            bool(job.get('uses')),
        )

    # A job-level group can supersede on a different key from the workflow-level one, which is how
    # two runs of a commit end up disagreeing again by a side door. One lane governs all of them.
    check(
        f"{name} declares no concurrency group of its own",
        not (job.get('concurrency') or {}),
    )

for name in sorted(guard_jobs - set(jobs)):
    check(f"declared guard job {name} still exists in the workflow", False)

# The lanes are also defeated one level down. A workflow the umbrella calls that declared its own
# group would claim it against the umbrella's -- deadlocking where the names match, and spanning
# both actions where they do not. Today none of them declares one, and that is exactly the kind of
# fact this file exists to stop being a comment.
called_locally = sorted({f for f in (called_workflow_file(job) for job in jobs.values()) if f})
for called in called_locally:
    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(workflow_path), called)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        check(f"{called} is a workflow in this repository", False)
        continue
    with open(path) as handle:
        check(
            f"{called} declares no concurrency of its own",
            not (yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}).get('concurrency'),
        )

# Every check has to be switchable off, or a plugin that cannot run one has no way out but to
# stop calling the umbrella entirely. A guard is the exception in both directions: it asserts a
# contract the caller can always satisfy, so it needs no way out, and offering one would let a
# caller keep the misconfiguration the guard exists to surface.
workflow_call = triggers.get('workflow_call') or {}
inputs = workflow_call.get('inputs') or {}
for name in jobs:
    if name in guard_jobs:
        check(f"{name} has no skip- input, being a guard and not a check", f"skip-{name}" not in inputs)
    elif name in opt_in_jobs:
        check(f"{name} has no skip- input, being opt in already", f"skip-{name}" not in inputs)
    else:
        check(f"{name} has a skip- input", f"skip-{name}" in inputs)

# An opt-in job that stopped consulting its input would run everywhere, which for verify-hook means
# failing every plugin that has not synced its hook -- most of them.
for name, input_name in sorted(opt_in_jobs.items()):
    if name not in jobs:
        check(f"declared opt-in job {name} still exists in the workflow", False)
        continue

    condition = str((jobs.get(name) or {}).get('if', ''))
    # Not a substring test: `!inputs.verify-hook` references the input and inverts the job, which
    # is the fleet-wide failure this is here to stop.
    check(
        f"{name} runs only when the caller sets {input_name}",
        re.search(r'(?<![!\w.-])inputs\.' + re.escape(input_name) + r'(?![\w-])', condition) is not None,
    )
    # And a default of true would redden every caller without a pull request against any of them.
    check(
        f"{input_name} defaults to not running {name}",
        (inputs.get(input_name) or {}).get('default') is False,
    )


# Keyed on the job by name rather than looped over every opt-in job, since a second opt-in job
# would have nothing to do with this script. The steps live in the called workflow now, so follow
# the `uses:` to them: asserting against the umbrella job would pass vacuously, and an empty list
# fails this closed if the call goes missing.
hook_called = called_workflow_file(jobs.get('hook-check'))
hook_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(workflow_path), hook_called) if hook_called else ''
hook_steps = []
if hook_path and os.path.isfile(hook_path):
    with open(hook_path) as handle:
        hook_doc = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}
    for hook_job in (hook_doc.get('jobs') or {}).values():
        hook_steps.extend(
            step for step in ((hook_job or {}).get('steps') or []) if isinstance(step, dict)
        )
check(
    f"hook-check runs {hook_script}",
    any(hook_script in str(step.get('run', '')) for step in hook_steps),
)

# And the umbrella's `with:` block is the only thing carrying a caller's workflows-ref pin into
# that workflow, which defaults it to main. Lose the line and the check silently compares a
# plugin's vendored hook against main's canonical copy rather than the pinned one -- so a plugin
# that pinned the ref precisely to hold an older hook steady goes red against a copy it
# deliberately did not take. The seam is new: the ref used to be inline in this file.
hook_with = ''.join(str(((jobs.get('hook-check') or {}).get('with') or {}).get('workflows-ref', '')).split())
check(
    "hook-check forwards workflows-ref to the called workflow",
    re.search(r'(?<![!\w.-])inputs\.workflows-ref(?![\w-])', hook_with) is not None,
)

# The compatibility workflow defaults all four to values that look right: dropping matomo-targets
# still checks both ends, but ignores a caller's per-target php, dropping php-version ignores the
# caller's compatibility-php-version, and dropping either ref runs main's generator or action
# against a caller that pinned an older one.
compatibility_with = (jobs.get('compatibility') or {}).get('with') or {}
for forwarded, source in (
    ('matomo-targets', 'matomo-targets'),
    ('php-version', 'compatibility-php-version'),
    ('scripts-ref', 'scripts-ref'),
    ('workflows-ref', 'workflows-ref'),
):
    value = ''.join(str(compatibility_with.get(forwarded, '')).split())
    check(
        f"compatibility forwards {source} to the called workflow as {forwarded}",
        re.search(r'(?<![!\w.-])inputs\.' + re.escape(source) + r'(?![\w-])', value) is not None,
    )

for name in sorted(pull_request_only):
    if name not in jobs:
        check(f"declared pull-request-only job {name} still exists in the workflow", False)
        continue
    condition = ''.join(str((jobs.get(name) or {}).get('if', '')).split())
    check(
        f"{name} runs only on a pull request",
        "github.event_name=='pull_request'" in condition,
    )

# Opt-out, not opt-in: a skip- input defaulting to true would leave a check running nowhere.
for name, spec in inputs.items():
    if name.startswith('skip-'):
        check(f"{name} defaults to running the check", spec.get('default') is False)

# The rules above only ever meet a document that complies, so an inverted or dead version of
# either would pass in silence. These drive them in both directions, the way the sibling guard
# tests drive theirs.
for label, job, expected in [
    ("an edited-action condition", {'if': "${{ !inputs.skip-phpcs && github.event.action != 'edited' }}"}, True),
    ("an action condition with other spacing", {'if': "${{ github.event.action=='edited' }}"}, True),
    ("an input-only condition", {'if': '${{ !inputs.skip-phpcs }}'}, False),
    ("an event-name condition", {'if': "${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}"}, False),
    ("no condition at all", {}, False),
]:
    check(
        f"rule one flags {label}" if expected else f"rule one passes {label}",
        conditions_on_event_action(job) is expected,
    )

for label, job, expected in [
    ("a job carrying an if:", {'if': '${{ inputs.verify-hook }}'}, True),
    ("a job carrying only needs:", {'needs': ['phpcs']}, True),
    ("a job carrying both", {'if': '${{ inputs.verify-hook }}', 'needs': ['phpcs']}, True),
    ("an unconditional job", {'runs-on': 'ubuntu-24.04'}, False),
]:
    check(
        f"rule two catches {label}" if expected else f"rule two exempts {label}",
        can_be_skipped(job) is expected,
    )

print()
print(f"{tests} tests, {len(failures)} failures")
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
PY

name: Hook check

# Fails when a plugin's vendored .git-hooks-matomo/pre-push differs from the canonical copy here.
#
# A called workflow rather than a job inside plugin-ci.yml, for a reason written where the
# caller can act on it: see the note above `hook-check` in plugin-ci.yml.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows to take the canonical hook and the comparison script from. This is this repository, so the workflow SHA is the right value when pinning."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'

# The job only reads the repository; everything else stays at none so any caller
# with default workflow permissions can use this without granting scopes.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  hook-check:
    name: Hook check
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      # Unique so it cannot collide with a directory the caller tracks.
      WORKFLOWS_DIR: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          lfs: false
          sparse-checkout: .git-hooks-matomo
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check the pre-push hook matches the canonical copy
        run: |
          # $WORKFLOWS_DIR is the caller's workflows-ref, which this repository's own README
          # encourages pinning. A pin predating this script would otherwise leave bash exiting 127
          # with no annotation -- a red check that analysed nothing and explains nothing.
          if [ ! -f "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_hook_sync.sh" ]; then
            echo "::error::workflows-ref does not carry scripts/bash/check_hook_sync.sh. Move that pin forward, or turn verify-hook off."
            exit 1
          fi

          bash "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_hook_sync.sh" "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/hooks/pre-push" .git-hooks-matomo/pre-push

name: PHPCS check

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plugin-name:
        description: "Name of the plugin, e.g. LoginLdap"
        required: true
        type: string
      php-version:
        description: "PHP version the job runs on. Accepts a literal version or one of the shared aliases (matomo5_min_php, matomo5_max_php, matomo6_min_php, matomo6_max_php), which track a Matomo major's floor and ceiling centrally. PHPCS needs at least 7.4, so matomo5_min_php is too low to use here."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo6_min_php'
      scripts-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/github-action-tests to take the version resolver from. Pinning the workflow does not pin this: pass a SHA from that repository, which is a different repository with different SHAs."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'

# The job only reads the repository; everything else stays at none so any caller
# with default workflow permissions can use this without granting scopes.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  phpcs:
    name: PHPCS
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Validate inputs
        env:
          PLUGIN_NAME: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
        run: |
          if [[ ! "$PLUGIN_NAME" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]]; then
            echo "Invalid plugin-name: $PLUGIN_NAME"
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          lfs: false
          persist-credentials: false
      # No GitHub context identifies the called workflow's own commit (verified
      # empirically: github.job_workflow_sha evaluates to empty), so pinning the
      # resolver is the caller's job via scripts-ref.
      - name: Check out github-action-tests repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/github-action-tests
          ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          # Unique name so it cannot collide with a directory the caller tracks
          path: .github-action-tests-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve PHP version
        id: resolve-php
        shell: bash
        env:
          PHP_VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.php-version }}
          SCRIPT_CHECKOUT: .github-action-tests-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: |
          RESOLVED_VERSION=$("$SCRIPT_CHECKOUT/scripts/bash/resolve_php_version.sh" "$PHP_VERSION_INPUT")

          # A plugin's phpcs.xml scans `.`, so anything left in the workspace is
          # linted as if it were the plugin's own code. Remove the checkout now
          # that the only thing it was needed for is done.
          rm -rf "$SCRIPT_CHECKOUT"

          echo "Resolved php-version '$PHP_VERSION_INPUT' to '$RESOLVED_VERSION'"
          echo "version=$RESOLVED_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Setup PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ steps.resolve-php.outputs.version }}
          tools: cs2pr
      # Installed outside the plugin on purpose. `composer init` in the workspace overwrites a
      # plugin's own composer.json -- verified: a file with real requires came back as
      # "require": {} -- and `composer install` would leave a vendor/ tree inside the very
      # directory the ruleset scans.
      - name: Install the coding standard
        env:
          TOOLS: ${{ runner.temp }}/phpcs-tools
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$TOOLS"
          cd "$TOOLS"
          composer init --name=matomo/phpcs-tools --quiet

      - name: Check PHP code styles

# release (plugin-dev-release.yml) dates it on the day it releases. Passes for every other plugin,
# so Plugins CI can run it everywhere and a plugin opts in by adopting the release workflow.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of this repository for the check script"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'

permissions:
  contents: read

  release-date:
    name: Release date
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read # read the plugin and list its tags
    env:
      # Unique so it cannot collide with a directory the caller tracks.
      WORKFLOWS_DIR: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}

name: AI Checklist

on:
  workflow_call: {}

# The gate reads the pull request description, and contents: read looks up the release tag below;
# callers must grant these three scopes in their own permissions block.
permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  AiChecklist:
    name: AI checklist gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      # The release date pull request plugin-dev-release.yml opens has no person to fill in the
      # checklist. It is recognised by its head being the commit its version was tagged at, which
      # only the workflow (or someone who can already push tags) makes, not by branch or author
      # names anyone can push. The job still runs and passes, so the gate's check is reported.
      - name: Recognise the release date pull request
        id: release-date
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          tagged=false
          if [[ "$HEAD_REF" =~ ^automated/release-date-([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)$ ]]; then
            version="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            if ! tag_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/ref/tags/$version" \
              --jq 'select(.object.type == "commit") | .object.sha' 2>&1); then
              # A missing tag is an ordinary pull request; any other failure would leave the date pull
              # request failing the gate with nothing saying why.
              [[ "$tag_sha" == *"HTTP 404"* ]] || echo "::warning::Could not look up the $version tag: $tag_sha"
              tag_sha=
            fi
            if [[ -n "$tag_sha" && "$tag_sha" == "$HEAD_SHA" ]]; then
              tagged=true
              echo "The head is the commit $version was released from, so the checklist is not required."
            fi
          fi
          echo "tagged=$tagged" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Run the checklist gate
        if: steps.release-date.outputs.tagged != 'true'
        uses: matomo-org/github-action-checklist-gate@d5f101a2538ef30ddb3b06cc366f852c9851b588 # main as of 2026-08-04

# Compiles a plugin's stylesheets and templates against both ends of the Matomo range its
# plugin.json declares.
#
# PHPStan cannot see either kind of dependency on core: a Less mixin or variable, or a Twig
# function, filter or tag, is resolved when the asset or template is compiled, so a plugin using
# one that its minimum Matomo does not have yet, or that its maximum no longer has, installs
# cleanly and then fails on every page that needs it. The minimum leg catches the first and the
# maximum leg the second.
#
# The tests doing the compiling are generated into the runner's Matomo checkout by
# scripts/bash/generate_compatibility_checks.sh and never reach the plugin repository.

name: Compatibility check

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plugin-name:
        description: "Name of the plugin, e.g. LoginLdap"
        required: true
        type: string
      dependent-plugins:
        description: "Space-separated repository slugs to check out, e.g. 'innocraft/plugin-Funnels'"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      php-version:
        description: "PHP version for a target that sets no `php` of its own. Accepts a literal version or one of the shared aliases (matomo5_min_php, matomo5_max_php, matomo6_min_php, matomo6_max_php). The default clears Matomo 6's floor of 8.1, which matomo5_min_php (7.2) cannot install."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo6_min_php'
      scripts-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/github-action-tests, whose composite action runs the tests. Pinning this workflow does not pin that: pass a SHA from that repository, which is a different repository with different SHAs."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows to take the test generator and its templates from. This is this repository, so the workflow SHA is the right value when pinning."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      matomo-targets:
        description: >-
          JSON array of {target, php} objects, one compilation run each. `php` is optional and
          falls back to the php-version input; set it per target when the targets span Matomo
          majors, because a Matomo 6 checkout cannot be installed on the PHP 7.2 that Matomo 5
          allows.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '[{"target": "minimum_required_matomo"}, {"target": "maximum_supported_matomo"}]'
    secrets:
      TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  compatibility:
    name: Compatibility (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.matomo-targets) }}
    env:
      PLUGIN_NAME: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
      DEPENDENT_PLUGINS: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins }}
      # Dot-prefixed so checkout_matomo.sh's `cp -R !($PLUGIN_NAME)` leaves it out of the plugin it
      # assembles: that glob enables extglob, not dotglob. Unique so it cannot collide with a
      # directory the caller tracks.
      WORKFLOWS_DIR: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    steps:
      - name: Validate inputs
        run: |
          if [[ ! "$PLUGIN_NAME" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]]; then
            echo "Invalid plugin-name: $PLUGIN_NAME"
            exit 1
          fi

          # checkout_dependent_plugins.sh does `rm -rf plugins/<derived-name>` before
          # cloning, so a dependent plugin resolving to the plugin under test would
          # silently replace it and compile the wrong code. Refuse instead.
          for slug in $DEPENDENT_PLUGINS; do
            name=${slug##*/}
            name=${name#plugin-}
            if [[ "$name" == "$PLUGIN_NAME" ]]; then
              echo "dependent-plugins entry '$slug' resolves to the plugin under test ($PLUGIN_NAME)."
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          lfs: false
          persist-credentials: false

      # Checked out and called as a local action because `uses:` takes no expression, so a remote
      # reference could follow neither scripts-ref nor the pinning check_action_pins.sh requires.
      # The path is fixed for the same reason, and dot-prefixed like WORKFLOWS_DIR.
      - name: Check out github-action-tests repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/github-action-tests
          ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          path: .plugin-ci-github-action-tests
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # The action runs setup-script as ${{ github.workspace }}/<path>, so the path stays relative,
      # and hands phpunit-test-options to run_tests.sh through an environment variable, so the `|`
      # is not a pipe. The filter has no spaces because that variable is expanded unquoted. The
      # generator also removes the token this passes, before PHPUnit runs the plugin's code, and
      # it is passed at all only when there are dependent plugins to clone with it.
      - name: Compile against ${{ matrix.target }}
        uses: ./.plugin-ci-github-action-tests
        with:
          test-type: PluginTests
          plugin-name: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
          matomo-test-branch: ${{ matrix.target }}
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php || inputs.php-version }}
          dependent-plugins: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins }}
          github-token: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins != '' && secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN || '' }}
          setup-script: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}/scripts/bash/generate_compatibility_checks.sh
          phpunit-test-options: --filter=GeneratedAssetCompilationTest|GeneratedTwigCompilationTest

      # Reads the markers the generated tests write, not a JUnit log: run_tests.sh appends its own
      # --log-junit on push runs, overriding any passed above.
      - name: Check both compatibility tests ran
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}/scripts/bash/check_compatibility_results.sh compatibility-results

# Parses a plugin's scoped dependencies against the oldest PHP that tree has to run on.
#
# `vendor/prefixed` is prefixed by matomo-scoper but not downgraded -- the scoper deliberately
# keeps attributes rather than rewriting them away, and ships no rector pass -- so the syntax in
# there is whatever composer resolved. Nothing else proves that resolution matched the plugin's
# floor: a file is only parsed when something loads it, so the tests reach whichever prefixed
# files they happen to exercise, and PHPStan need not reach them at all (GoogleAnalyticsImporter
# puts `vendor/` under excludePaths.analyse so the prefixed tree does not drown its report).
#
# The floor is derived rather than pinned, because it differs per plugin and per branch, and
# composer.json governs it -- see scripts/bash/resolve_plugin_min_php.sh for the precedence and
# why plugin.json alone is the wrong source.

name: Minimum PHP lint

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      lint-path:
        description: "Directory to parse. Skipped when it does not exist, so this is safe to run on a plugin that ships no scoped dependencies."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'vendor/prefixed'
      php-version:
        description: "Override the floor derived from the plugin's composer.json and plugin.json. Accepts a major.minor version such as 8.1, or one of the shared aliases. Leave unset unless the declared floor is wrong."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      scripts-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/github-action-tests to take the version resolver from. Pinning this workflow does not pin that: pass a SHA from that repository, which is a different repository with different SHAs."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of this repository to take the plugin floor resolver from."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  min-php-lint:
    name: Lint scoped dependencies on minimum PHP
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          lfs: false
          # Only the tree being parsed. Cone mode brings the root files regardless, which is
          # where composer.json and plugin.json are read from. A plugin with no scoped
          # dependencies then clones almost nothing, which is most of them.
          sparse-checkout: ${{ inputs.lint-path }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # Checked before anything is installed: most plugins ship no scoped dependencies, and the
      # whole job is then a few seconds rather than a PHP setup they never use.
      - name: Look for scoped dependencies
        id: look
        shell: bash
        env:
          LINT_PATH: ${{ inputs.lint-path }}
        run: |
          if [ -d "$LINT_PATH" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            # A notice rather than a log line: this is the supported no-op for most plugins, but
            # it is also what a mistyped or newly-gitignored lint-path looks like, and that would
            # otherwise be green across the fleet with nothing to see.
            echo "::notice::No $LINT_PATH directory; nothing to lint."
            echo "No $LINT_PATH directory; nothing to lint." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # Only needed to derive the floor, so skipped entirely when a caller supplies one.
      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        if: ${{ steps.look.outputs.present == 'true' && inputs.php-version == '' }}
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # No GitHub context identifies the called workflow's own commit (verified empirically:
      # github.job_workflow_sha evaluates to empty), so pinning the resolvers is the caller's
      # job via scripts-ref and workflows-ref.
      - name: Check out github-action-tests repository
        if: ${{ steps.look.outputs.present == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/github-action-tests
          ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          path: .github-action-tests-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve the plugin's minimum PHP
        id: resolve
        if: ${{ steps.look.outputs.present == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          PHP_VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.php-version }}
          WORKFLOWS_REF: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          SCRIPTS_REF: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          WORKFLOWS_CHECKOUT: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          SCRIPTS_CHECKOUT: .github-action-tests-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$PHP_VERSION_INPUT" ]; then
            floor="$PHP_VERSION_INPUT"
            source='the php-version override'
            echo "Using the php-version override: $floor"
          else
            # A pinned workflows-ref predating this script would otherwise fail as a bare 127.
            RESOLVER="$WORKFLOWS_CHECKOUT/scripts/bash/resolve_plugin_min_php.sh"
            if [ ! -f "$RESOLVER" ]; then
              echo "::error::workflows-ref '$WORKFLOWS_REF' does not carry scripts/bash/resolve_plugin_min_php.sh. Pin a ref that has it, or pass php-version."
              exit 1
            fi
            notes=$(mktemp)
            if ! floor=$(bash "$RESOLVER" . 2>"$notes"); then
              sed 's/^/::error::/' "$notes"
              rm -f "$notes"
              exit 1
            fi
            # Promoted to an annotation: the resolver calls a disagreement between the manifests
            # the defect itself, and as plain stderr it was the least visible thing the job emits.
            sed 's/^Manifests disagree/::warning::Manifests disagree/' "$notes"
            source=$(sed -n 's/^Floor from \(.*\): .*/\1/p' "$notes" | head -1)
            rm -f "$notes"
          fi

          # resolve_php_version.sh turns an alias into a version and passes anything else through
          # unchanged, so an alias it does not know -- a Matomo major newer than its table --
          # would arrive at setup-php verbatim. Fail on it here rather than there.
          ALIAS_RESOLVER="$SCRIPTS_CHECKOUT/scripts/bash/resolve_php_version.sh"
          if [ ! -f "$ALIAS_RESOLVER" ]; then
            echo "::error::scripts-ref '$SCRIPTS_REF' does not carry scripts/bash/resolve_php_version.sh."
            exit 1
          fi
          version=$("$ALIAS_RESOLVER" "$floor")
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::'$floor' is not a usable PHP version. Pass a major.minor version such as 8.1, or a shared alias the table knows."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Removed before the lint so a helper checkout can never be mistaken for the plugin's
          # own code, the way a checkout left in the workspace is picked up by a phpcs.xml
          # scanning `.`.
          rm -rf "$WORKFLOWS_CHECKOUT" "$SCRIPTS_CHECKOUT"

          echo "Linting against PHP $version, from ${source:-an unknown source}"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "source=${source:-an unknown source}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Setup PHP
        if: ${{ steps.look.outputs.present == 'true' }}
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.version }}

      - name: Lint
        if: ${{ steps.look.outputs.present == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          LINT_PATH: ${{ inputs.lint-path }}
          PHP_VERSION: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.version }}
          PHP_VERSION_SOURCE: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.source }}
        run: |
          # Collected rather than streamed: the exit status of a process substitution is
          # discarded, so a find that failed partway would leave a green check over a partial
          # tree -- the same silence the empty-directory warning below exists to prevent.
          listing=$(mktemp)
          # -H, because the probe above uses `[ -d ]`, which follows a symlink, while a bare
          # `find` does not follow a symlinked starting point. A committed `vendor/prefixed`
          # symlink would otherwise probe as present, list nothing, and fail with "contains no PHP
          # files. Check lint-path" -- pointing the maintainer at the one thing that is correct.
          if ! find -H "$LINT_PATH" -type f -name '*.php' > "$listing"; then
            echo "::error::Could not list PHP files under $LINT_PATH."
            exit 1
          fi

          status=0
          files=0
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            files=$(( files + 1 ))
            if ! error=$(php -l "$file" 2>&1); then
              # A workflow command is parsed one line at a time, and php -l emits the parse error
              # plus a trailing summary line, so the rest would fall out of the annotation.
              # % first: GitHub unescapes %25 too, so escaping newlines first would let a literal
              # %0A in the message come back out as a real newline.
              escaped="${error//%/%25}"
              echo "::error file=${file}::${escaped//$'\n'/%0A}"
              status=1
            fi
          done < "$listing"
          rm -f "$listing"

          # Failing rather than warning, because a green check that parsed nothing reads as
          # coverage. An absent directory is the supported no-op and skips earlier; a directory
          # that exists and holds no PHP means lint-path is stale or mistyped.
          if [ "$files" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::$LINT_PATH contains no PHP files, so nothing was linted. Check lint-path."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Parsed $files file(s) against PHP $PHP_VERSION."


          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Scoped dependencies do not parse on PHP $PHP_VERSION, taken from $PHP_VERSION_SOURCE."
            echo "The scoper prefixes but does not downgrade, so re-running it changes nothing."
            echo "Either the tree was resolved too high -- lower config.platform.php in"
            echo "composer.json, or the platform-php passed to the vendored dependencies update,"
            echo "and re-resolve -- or the declared floor is stale, in which case"
            echo "raise require.php in plugin.json to what the tree actually needs."
          fi
          exit "$status"

name: Timezone safety

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plugin-name:
        description: "Name of the plugin, e.g. LoginLdap"
        required: true
        type: string
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows to take the checker from. This is this repository, so the workflow SHA is the right value when pinning."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      timezone-test-command:

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      skip-static-scan:
        description: "Do not run the timezone safety static scan; useful when the umbrella workflow already provides it."
        required: false
        type: boolean

        description: "Why this plugin needs no timezone regression suite although it has date or site-timezone logic. Empty means it is not exempt. Read by the static scan job, so it has no effect with skip-static-scan."

        type: string
        default: ''

  contents: read

jobs:
  timezone-safety:

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          # fail only on findings added by a change while still printing older findings for cleanup.
          fetch-depth: 0
          lfs: false
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run timezone safety scan
        shell: bash
        env:
          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          EVENT_BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
          WORKFLOWS_REF: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
        run: |
          # workflows-ref is often pinned independently from this workflow. A stale pin must fail
          # closed rather than produce a green job without running the safety scan; callers can
          # explicitly opt out with skip-static-scan (skip-timezone-safety in the Plugins CI umbrella)
          # while advancing the pin.
          if [ ! -f "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_timezone_safety.sh" ]; then
            echo "::error::workflows-ref '$WORKFLOWS_REF' does not carry scripts/bash/check_timezone_safety.sh; update workflows-ref or skip this reusable workflow with skip-static-scan (the Plugins CI umbrella uses skip-timezone-safety)."
            exit 2
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/run_timezone_safety_workflow.sh" ]; then
            echo "::error::workflows-ref '$WORKFLOWS_REF' does not carry scripts/bash/run_timezone_safety_workflow.sh; update workflows-ref or skip this reusable workflow with skip-static-scan (the Plugins CI umbrella uses skip-timezone-safety)."
            exit 2
          fi
          checker="$RUNNER_TEMP/check_timezone_safety.sh"
          runner="$RUNNER_TEMP/run_timezone_safety_workflow.sh"
          cp "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_timezone_safety.sh" "$checker"
          cp "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/run_timezone_safety_workflow.sh" "$runner"
          # Optional here: the coverage step reports a pin without it, by its own rollout rule.
          if [ -f "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_timezone_regression_coverage.sh" ]; then
            cp "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_timezone_regression_coverage.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/check_timezone_regression_coverage.sh"
          fi
          rm -rf "$WORKFLOWS_DIR"
          bash "$runner" "$checker"

      - name: Check timezone regression coverage
        # Reported even when the scan fails, so one run shows both verdicts.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          WORKFLOWS_REF: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          TIMEZONE_REGRESSION_EXEMPT: ${{ inputs.timezone-regression-exempt }}
          # warn until every plugin that needs the regression suite runs it or is exempt; enforce
          # then fails a pull request, while pushes and dispatches stay advisory like the scan.
          COVERAGE_MODE: warn
        run: |
          enforcing=false
          if [ "$COVERAGE_MODE" = enforce ] && [ -n "$BASE_BRANCH" ]; then
            enforcing=true
          fi
          # A check that cannot run fails only where a verdict would, so the rollout stays advisory.
          not_checked() {
            if [ "$enforcing" = true ]; then
              echo "::error::$1"
              exit 2
            fi
            echo "::warning::$1"
            exit 0
          }
          coverage="$RUNNER_TEMP/check_timezone_regression_coverage.sh"
          if [ ! -f "$coverage" ]; then
            # Caller input: flattened so a newline cannot start a workflow command.
            ref=$(tr -s '\r\n' ' ' <<< "$WORKFLOWS_REF" | sed 's/ $//')
