            not_checked "Timezone regression coverage was not checked: the scan step did not stage scripts/bash/check_timezone_regression_coverage.sh, either because it did not run or because workflows-ref '$ref' predates the script."
          fi
          # apt rather than pip, for the same reasons as in this repository's own tests workflow.
          # -P, so a yaml.py in the plugin cannot pass for PyYAML.
          if ! python3 -P -c 'import yaml' 2>/dev/null; then
            { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-yaml; } > /dev/null \
              || not_checked 'Timezone regression coverage was not checked: PyYAML could not be installed.'
          fi
          args=()
          if [ "$enforcing" = true ]; then
            args+=(--enforce)
          fi
          status=0
          bash "$coverage" "${args[@]}" . || status=$?
          if [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; then
            not_checked 'Timezone regression coverage was not checked: the check could not run; see the error above.'
          fi
          exit "$status"

  timezone-regression:
    name: Timezone regression suite (${{ inputs.plugin-name }})
    if: ${{ inputs.timezone-test-command != '' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # A caller supplies a targeted command; allow a genuinely long suite without making the
    # static scan wait for it. Repositories should keep this command focused on timezone cases.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    # These environment variables are hints for the caller command; the reusable workflow does
    # not provision PHP or MySQL, so the command remains responsible for applying them.
    env:
      TZ: Pacific/Auckland
      MYSQL_TIMEZONE: Pacific/Auckland
      TIMEZONE_TEST_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.timezone-test-command }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          lfs: false
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run targeted timezone regression suite
        shell: bash
        run: bash -eo pipefail -c "$TIMEZONE_TEST_COMMAND"

name: Codex Review

# The review logic — preflight, prompt, schema and posting — lives in composite actions in
# innocraft/github-action-tests-private and is checked out here with TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN. It cannot
# be called as a reusable workflow instead: GitHub resolves those from the callee repository's
# Actions access policy at parse time, which cannot grant a public caller access to a private
# repository. This workflow is the job structure that policy will not let a plugin repository
# import, so that a plugin repository only has to name itself.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plugin-name:
        description: "Name of the plugin, e.g. LoginLdap. Passing it from the caller keeps the name out of the untrusted pull request; when empty the review reads it from plugin.json instead."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      trigger-label:
        description: "Pull request label that triggers the review. The caller gates on this label in its own `if:` condition, so both have to change together."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'codex-review'
      allowed-owners:
        description: "Comma-separated repository owners allowed to run a review"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo-org,innocraft'
      automation-paths:
        description: "Newline- or comma-separated caller-repository paths that must receive human review before Codex runs. Entries ending in / match by prefix."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: |
          .github/workflows/codex-review.yml
          .github/codex/
      review-actions-ref:
        description: "Ref of the review actions repository to run. When pinning this workflow to a SHA, pin the actions to a SHA too."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      matomo-agent-skills-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/matomo-agent-skills to install before running Codex"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      matomo-core-repository:
        description: "Matomo core repository checked out for read-only review context"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo-org/matomo'
      matomo-core-ref:
        description: "Matomo core ref checked out for read-only review context. The default derives it from the pull request base branch, so a plugin PR against 6.x-dev is reviewed against 6.x core; set a literal ref to override."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'auto'
      codex-model:
        description: "OpenAI model passed to openai/codex-action. Override only to move off the default."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'gpt-5.6-sol'
      codex-effort:
        description: "Reasoning effort passed to openai/codex-action: minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'xhigh'
    secrets:
      OPENAI_API_KEY:
        [REDACTED] "OpenAI API key used by openai/codex-action"
        required: true
      TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        [REDACTED] "Token with read access to the review actions repository. A caller's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read a private repository."
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: none

# In a reusable workflow ${{ github.workflow }} resolves to the CALLER's workflow name, so a group
# built from it collides with a caller group of the same name and GitHub cancels the run with
# "a deadlock was detected for concurrency group ...". Use a static prefix unique to this workflow.
concurrency:
  group: codex-review-shared-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  preflight:
    if: ${{ github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == inputs.trigger-label }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      should_run: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.should_run }}
      safety_failure: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.safety_failure }}
      safety_message: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.safety_message }}
      skip_reason: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.skip_reason }}
      skip_message: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.skip_message }}
      changed_files: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.changed_files }}
      automation_files: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.automation_files }}
      base_sha: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.base_sha }}
      head_sha: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.head_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify review actions token is configured
        env:
          TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN}" ]; then
            echo "::error::TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN is empty. It must hold a token with read access to innocraft/github-action-tests-private, because the calling repository's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read a private repository. Scope the organization secret to the calling repository." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Checkout trusted review actions
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: innocraft/github-action-tests-private
          ref: ${{ inputs.review-actions-ref }}
          token: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          path: github-action-tests
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Preflight
        id: preflight
        uses: ./github-action-tests/review/actions/preflight
        with:
          allowed-owners: ${{ inputs.allowed-owners }}
          automation-paths: ${{ inputs.automation-paths }}

  codex:
    needs: preflight
    if: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.should_run == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout trusted review actions
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: innocraft/github-action-tests-private
          ref: ${{ inputs.review-actions-ref }}
          token: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          path: github-action-tests
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run Codex review
        uses: ./github-action-tests/review/actions/codex
        with:
          openai-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          base-sha: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.base_sha }}
          head-sha: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.head_sha }}
          changed-files: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.changed_files }}
          matomo-agent-skills-ref: ${{ inputs.matomo-agent-skills-ref }}
          matomo-core-repository: ${{ inputs.matomo-core-repository }}
          matomo-core-ref: ${{ inputs.matomo-core-ref }}
          plugin-name: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
          codex-model: ${{ inputs.codex-model }}
          codex-effort: ${{ inputs.codex-effort }}

  post-review:
    needs: [preflight, codex]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == inputs.trigger-label }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      actions: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout trusted review actions
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: innocraft/github-action-tests-private
          ref: ${{ inputs.review-actions-ref }}
          token: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          path: github-action-tests
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Post review result
        uses: ./github-action-tests/review/actions/post-review
        with:
          codex-result: ${{ needs.codex.result }}
          preflight-result: ${{ needs.preflight.result }}
          safety-failure: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.safety_failure }}
          safety-message: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.safety_message }}
          skip-reason: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.skip_reason }}
          skip-message: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.skip_message }}
          reviewed-base-sha: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.base_sha }}
          reviewed-head-sha: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.head_sha }}

  cleanup:
    needs: [preflight, codex, post-review]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == inputs.trigger-label }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      # Inline and checkout-free on purpose. Every other job needs the trusted-actions checkout, so
      # a missing or invalid TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN fails all of them; a cleanup that needed the same
      # checkout would fail with them and strand the trigger label on the pull request, with no
      # review and nothing explaining why. Removing a label is not review logic.
      - name: Remove trigger label
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        env:
          TRIGGER_LABEL: ${{ inputs.trigger-label }}
        with:
          script: |
            const pr = context.payload.pull_request;
            try {
              await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: pr.number,
                name: process.env.TRIGGER_LABEL,
              });
            } catch (error) {
              if (error.status === 404) {
                core.info(`${process.env.TRIGGER_LABEL} label was already removed.`);
                return;
              }
              if (error.status === 403) {
                core.warning(`Could not remove ${process.env.TRIGGER_LABEL} label because this workflow token lacks permission.`);
                return;
              }
              throw error;
            }

# Dispatches a plugin's build for every maintained branch that is not its default one.
#
# GitHub only ever runs `schedule` from the default branch's copy of a workflow file, so the
# moment a plugin's default flips (5.x-dev -> 6.x-dev) the older line stops being built and
# nothing says so. This closes that gap from inside the plugin repository: `workflow_dispatch`
# is a documented exception to the rule that GITHUB_TOKEN-triggered events create no workflow
# run, so the caller's own token is enough and no PAT or cross-repository App is involved.
#
# Dispatching, rather than building another branch's source from a central definition, is what
# keeps the result correct and legible: the run uses the target branch's own workflow file --
# whose test matrix genuinely differs per branch -- and it is attributed to the branch it built,
# which is what the plugin build dashboard's per-branch badges read.
#
# The caller keeps two things that cannot move here. The `schedule` trigger, because a reusable
# workflow's own cron would fire in this repository rather than the plugin's; and the
# `actions: write` grant, because permissions can only be maintained or reduced down a call
# chain, never elevated, so a caller that does not grant it leaves the dispatch unauthorised.
#
# One bound on the guarantee: GitHub disables scheduled workflows in a public repository after
# 60 days without repository activity, which a branch in pure maintenance can reach. The
# `activity` job fails ahead of that so a person can act; it deliberately does not keep the
# schedule alive itself (see the job).

name: Branch sweep

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      maintained-branches:
        description: >-
          Whitespace-separated branches to keep built, whichever of them is not the default,
          so a YAML block scalar works as well as a single line.
          Deliberately an explicit list rather than every `*.x-dev` branch a repository has:
          most still carry dead 2.x-dev, 3.x-dev and 4.x-dev lines. Dispatching 4.x-dev queues
          for 24 hours and then auto-cancels, because its workflow requests a runner label that
          no longer exists, and the older two carry no test workflow at all.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '6.x-dev 5.x-dev'
      workflow-file:
        description: "Workflow file to dispatch in the plugin repository"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo-tests.yml'

permissions:
  actions: write # dispatch the plugin's build workflow
  contents: read # read the default branch name, check a branch exists and has the workflow file

# Queued rather than superseded, because losing a sweep is losing a week of builds for that
# branch. Cancelling would be the wrong trade even though the job is seconds long. (Queueing does
# not stop a manual run and the schedule both dispatching -- the second sweep runs moments later
# and re-dispatches -- but a re-dispatched build simply replaces the cancelled one.)
#
# Named without ${{ github.workflow }}: in a reusable workflow that resolves to the CALLER's
# workflow name, which collides with a caller group of the same name and GitHub then cancels the
# run for a concurrency deadlock.
concurrency:
  group: plugin-branch-sweep
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  sweep:
    name: Dispatch builds for non-default branches
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # `gh workflow run` resolves its target repository from GH_REPO or a git remote, and this
          # job deliberately checks nothing out. GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not consulted. The `gh api`
          # calls below need none of this, because their paths are already fully qualified.
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          MAINTAINED_BRANCHES: ${{ inputs.maintained-branches }}
          WORKFLOW_FILE: ${{ inputs.workflow-file }}
        run: |
          # Runs a command up to three times, emitting only the successful attempt's output.
          # That last part is load-bearing: gh writes a failed response body to stdout, with no
          # trailing newline, so returning every attempt's output would let a 404 body run
          # straight into the real answer on one line. A default branch read as that garbage
          # matches no branch name, so the real default would be dispatched too -- the double
          # build this design exists to avoid. RETRY_ERROR carries the last failure's output.
          #
          # $1 is a pattern that ends it early, for the failures that will never come good:
          # backing off three times over a branch that does not exist, or a ref that carries no
          # workflow_dispatch trigger, is pure delay and two misleading log lines.
          retry_unless() {
            # $stop is expanded unquoted below, so it has to be a bare glob: quotes inside it
            # would be matched as literal characters instead of quoting the pattern, which is
            # what they do in an inline `case`.
            local stop="$1" attempt out errors
            shift
            RETRY_ERROR=''
            errors=$(mktemp)
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              # stderr is captured separately rather than merged: the default-branch read consumes
              # what this emits, so an otherwise successful gh writing a warning there -- a token
              # precedence or scope notice, say -- would arrive spliced onto the branch name.
              if out=$("$@" 2>"$errors"); then
                printf '%s\n' "$out"
                rm -f "$errors"
                return 0
              fi
              # Both streams matter on failure: gh puts the message on stderr and the response
              # body on stdout, and the stop pattern is matched against the message.
              RETRY_ERROR="$(cat "$errors")$out"
              if [ -n "$stop" ]; then
                # shellcheck disable=SC2254 # $stop is a glob pattern by design
                case "$RETRY_ERROR" in
                  $stop) rm -f "$errors"; return 1 ;;
                esac
              fi
              echo "Attempt $attempt of 3 failed: $*" >&2
              if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
                sleep $(( attempt * 5 ))
              fi
            done
            rm -f "$errors"
            return 1
          }

          # Read from the API rather than github.event.repository.default_branch, which only the
          # payload-carrying triggers supply: workflow_call makes this callable from any of them.
          if ! default=$(retry_unless '' gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --jq .default_branch); then
            echo "::error::Could not read the default branch, so nothing was dispatched: $RETRY_ERROR"
            exit 1
          fi

          # --jq prints the string "null" for a field the response does not carry, and anything
          # spliced onto the answer carries characters a git ref cannot. All three read as a name
          # matching no branch, which would leave the real default dispatched alongside the rest.
          case "${default:-}" in
            ''|null|*[!A-Za-z0-9._/+-]*)
              echo "::error::Could not read the default branch, so nothing was dispatched."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

          # The caller runs from the default branch, so the file is missing there only when
          # workflow-file is wrong. Without this, every branch would be skipped as unadopted.
          if ! retry_unless '*HTTP 404*' \
            gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/contents/.github/workflows/$WORKFLOW_FILE?ref=$default" --jq .sha >/dev/null; then
            case "$RETRY_ERROR" in
              *"HTTP 404"*) echo "::error::Could not find .github/workflows/$WORKFLOW_FILE on $default, so nothing was dispatched. Check workflow-file." ;;
              *) echo "::error::Could not check whether $default has $WORKFLOW_FILE, so nothing was dispatched: $RETRY_ERROR" ;;
            esac
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Default branch is $default; its own schedule builds it."

          # Unquoted on purpose, so the list splits on newlines as well as spaces: the input is a
          # string, and a caller writing it as a YAML block scalar is natural. `read -ra` takes
          # only the first line of a here-string, which would silently drop every branch after
          # the first -- a branch quietly not being built, through this workflow's own input.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2206
          branches=( $MAINTAINED_BRANCHES )
          dispatched=0
          absent=0
          failed=0

          for branch in "${branches[@]}"; do
            if [ "$branch" = "$default" ]; then
              continue
            fi

            # A failure must not stop the loop: one bad branch starving every branch after it is
            # exactly how the previous central sweep went unnoticed for two weekends.
            if ! retry_unless '*HTTP 404*' \
              gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/branches/$branch" --jq .name >/dev/null; then
              # Only a 404 means the branch is genuinely absent. Reading every error as absence
              # would report a rate limit or an outage as "nothing to do" and leave the run green.
              case "$RETRY_ERROR" in
                *"HTTP 404"*)
                  echo "::notice::Skipping $branch: it is listed as maintained but does not exist here."
                  absent=$(( absent + 1 ))
                  ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::Could not check whether $branch exists: $RETRY_ERROR"
                  failed=1
                  ;;
              esac
              continue
            fi

            # A branch that has not adopted the workflow yet is not a failure. Dispatching it would
            # be refused with a 422 that reads the same as a file missing its trigger, so look first.
            if ! retry_unless '*HTTP 404*' \
              gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/contents/.github/workflows/$WORKFLOW_FILE?ref=$branch" --jq .sha >/dev/null; then
              case "$RETRY_ERROR" in
                *"HTTP 404"*)
                  echo "::notice::Skipping $branch: it has no .github/workflows/$WORKFLOW_FILE."
                  absent=$(( absent + 1 ))
                  ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::Could not check whether $branch has $WORKFLOW_FILE: $RETRY_ERROR"
                  failed=1
                  ;;
              esac
              continue
            fi

            if retry_unless '*HTTP 422*' gh workflow run "$WORKFLOW_FILE" --ref "$branch" >/dev/null; then
              echo "Dispatched $WORKFLOW_FILE on $branch."
              # Not (( dispatched++ )), which evaluates to the pre-increment 0 and so exits
              # non-zero on the first success, killing the step under `bash -e`.
              dispatched=$(( dispatched + 1 ))
            else
              echo "::error::Could not dispatch $WORKFLOW_FILE on $branch: $RETRY_ERROR"
              failed=1
            fi
          done

          # A run that dispatches nothing looks exactly like a working one, so say so -- but only
          # when an absent branch does not already explain it. A plugin with a single maintained
          # line reaches this every week by design, and warning at it weekly is how the annotation
          # stops being read. Naming nothing but the default is a real misconfiguration.
          if [ "$dispatched" -eq 0 ] && [ "$failed" -eq 0 ] && [ "$absent" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::warning::No non-default maintained branch was dispatched. Check maintained-branches ($MAINTAINED_BRANCHES) against the branches this repository has."
          fi

          exit "$failed"

  # Fails, rather than annotating, because a warning on a green scheduled run reaches nobody: a
  # failure notifies the user who last modified the caller's cron. A separate job so that it
  # neither blocks the dispatch nor is skipped when the dispatch fails.
  #
  # Keeping the schedule alive automatically, by commits or by re-enabling the workflow through
  # the API, is ruled out: GitHub disabled gautamkrishnar/keepalive-workflow for circumventing
  # the 60-day policy, so the remedy here is left to a person.
  activity:
    name: Fail before the schedule is disabled for inactivity
    permissions:
      contents: read # read the repository and its default branch's last commit
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Check repository activity
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # Two weekly runs of notice before day 60, with a missed run to spare.
          fail_after_days=45

          # Runs a command up to three times, leaving the successful attempt's output in OUT, or
          # the last failure's message and body. stderr is kept apart on success for the same
          # reason as in the sweep job: a gh warning would arrive spliced onto the answer.
          retry() {
            local attempt errors
            errors=$(mktemp)
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              if OUT=$("$@" 2>"$errors"); then
                rm -f "$errors"
                return 0
              fi
              OUT="$(cat "$errors")$OUT"
              if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
                sleep $(( attempt * 5 ))
              fi
            done
            rm -f "$errors"
            return 1
          }

          if ! retry gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --jq '"\(.private) \(.default_branch)"'; then
            echo "::error::Could not read the repository, so its activity was not checked: $OUT"
            exit 1
          fi
          read -r private default <<<"$OUT"

          if [ "$private" = true ]; then
            echo "Private repository: GitHub only disables a public repository's schedules for inactivity."
            exit 0
          fi
          case "${default:-}" in
            ''|null|*[!A-Za-z0-9._/+-]*)
              echo "::error::Could not read the default branch, so its activity was not checked."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

          # The sweep dispatches the caller on the other maintained branches too, and each of
          # those runs would otherwise repeat the same failure.
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" != "$default" ]; then
            echo "Running on $GITHUB_REF_NAME; the run on $default checks activity."
            exit 0
          fi

          # GitHub does not document what counts as activity. A commit on the default branch is
          # the one reported to reset the count, so it is the conservative measure.
          if ! retry gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$default" --jq .commit.committer.date; then
            echo "::error::Could not read the last commit on $default, so its activity was not checked: $OUT"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! last=$(date -d "$OUT" +%s 2>/dev/null); then
            echo "::error::Could not read the date of the last commit on $default ('$OUT'), so its activity was not checked."
            exit 1
          fi
          days=$(( ($(date +%s) - last) / 86400 ))

          if [ "$days" -ge "$fail_after_days" ]; then
            echo "::error::The last commit on $default was $days days ago. GitHub disables a public repository's scheduled workflows after 60 days without activity, which stops this workflow and the plugin's other schedules without saying so. Merge outstanding maintenance to $default, or re-enable the workflows in the Actions tab once GitHub has disabled them."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "The last commit on $default was $days days ago."

# Releases plugin.json's version from the N.x-dev branch the caller runs on, or the caller's
# release-branch, when it has no tag yet.
#
# Its CHANGELOG.md entry is merged undated or Unreleased (Plugins CI's release date check fails one
# dated by hand). This dates it on automated/release-date-<version>, tags and publishes that commit,
# then opens a pull request bringing the date into the branch and sets it to merge once the branch
# protection's required checks pass, if it lets this token or the approver token do so. Otherwise
# the pull request is left open for a person, with a warning; the release never waits on that merge.
#
# The caller owns the triggers: a weekly schedule, workflow_dispatch, and plugin-branch-sweep.yml to
# dispatch it on the other maintained branch, since a schedule only runs on the default branch.

name: Plugin development release

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of this repository for the release scripts. This is this repository, so the workflow SHA is the right value when pinning."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      reviewer-team:
        description: "Slug of the team in the repository's organisation that a release date pull request left waiting on a person requests review from, or mentions without approver-token. Empty picks plugin-reviewers in matomo-org and premium-plugins-reviewers in innocraft."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      skip-ci-check:
        description: "Release even when a push CI run on the branch's head failed or is still running. For a run by hand when that failure is not the release's concern; leave it false on the schedule."
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ci-wait-minutes:
        description: "How long to wait, from 0 to 45 minutes, for push CI still running on the branch's head before failing without a release."
        required: false
        type: number
        default: 45
      release-branch:
        description: "Release from this one branch instead of N.x-dev, with no check that plugin.json's major matches it. For a plugin that keeps a single branch and versions apart from Matomo, such as a bundle. Empty releases only from N.x-dev. Give a literal, quoted branch name: Plugins CI's release-date job fails on an expression."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      require-approver-token:
        [REDACTED] "Fail before releasing when approver-token is empty, so a secret that was renamed, removed or not passed under secrets: is noticed rather than the release date pull request being left for a person."
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
    secrets:
      approver-token:
        [REDACTED] "Optional token for a user other than github-actions, which approves and merges the release date pull request where the branch protection needs a review or restricts who can push, and requests the team review on one left waiting on a person. A GitHub App needs organisation Members read access for that."
        required: false

permissions: {}

# Queued rather than cancelled, so a dispatch during the scheduled run cannot interrupt a release
# halfway. Named without ${{ github.workflow }}, which resolves to the caller's workflow name here.
concurrency:
  group: plugin-dev-release-${{ github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      actions: write # approve the held checks on the release date pull request
      contents: write # push the release date branch and the tag, publish the release
      pull-requests: write # open and merge the release date pull request
    # ci-wait-minutes, at most 45, plus the release and any earlier versions it finishes.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Unique so it cannot collide with a directory the caller tracks.
      WORKFLOWS_DIR: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    steps:
      - name: Check the approver token
        if: inputs.require-approver-token
        env:
          # Whether it is set, never the token, which only the merge step is given.
          HAS_APPROVER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.approver-token != '' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "$HAS_APPROVER_TOKEN" != true ]]; then
            echo "::error::require-approver-token is set but approver-token is empty, so nothing was released. Check that the caller passes it under secrets: and that the secret exists."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # The guard fails closed without PyYAML; see plugin-ci.yml for why the install is conditional.
      - name: Install the YAML parser the guard needs
        shell: bash
        run: python3 -P -c 'import yaml' || { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-yaml; }

      - name: Check caller concurrency
        env:
          WORKFLOW_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bash "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash/check_caller_concurrency.sh" "$WORKFLOW_REF" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            "plugin-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/plugin-dev-release.yml"

      - name: Stage release scripts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-scripts"
          cp -r "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/bash" "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/scripts/python" "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-scripts/"
          echo "RELEASE_SCRIPTS=$RUNNER_TEMP/release-scripts" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          # Keep the shared checkout out of the plugin repository before git records the release.
          rm -rf "$WORKFLOWS_DIR"

      - name: Configure git credentials
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # git asks the helper, which reads the runner-masked token itself, so no value derived from
          # the token reaches the environment and needs masking.
          {
            echo "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1"
            echo "GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.https://github.com.helper"
            echo "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo \"password=[REDACTED]"; }; f"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Prepare release
        id: prepare
        env:
          RELEASE_SKIP_CI_CHECK: ${{ inputs.skip-ci-check }}
          RELEASE_CI_WAIT_MINUTES: ${{ inputs.ci-wait-minutes }}
          RELEASE_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.release-branch }}
        shell: bash
        run: bash "$RELEASE_SCRIPTS/bash/prepare_plugin_dev_release.sh" "$GITHUB_REF"

      - name: Date the release
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.release_needed == 'true'
        env:
          TODAY: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.today }}
        shell: bash
        run: bash "$RELEASE_SCRIPTS/bash/push_plugin_release_date.sh" "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$TODAY"

      - name: Create release tag
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.release_needed == 'true'
        env:
          TODAY: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.today }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.version }}
        shell: bash
        run: bash "$RELEASE_SCRIPTS/bash/tag_plugin_dev_release.sh" "$VERSION" "$TODAY"

      - name: Create GitHub release
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.publish_needed == 'true'
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          FINISH: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.finish }}
          PLUGIN_NAME: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.plugin_name }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          # One version failing must not hold back the versions after it.
          status=0
          for release in $FINISH; do
            bash "$RELEASE_SCRIPTS/bash/publish_plugin_release.sh" "$PLUGIN_NAME" "${release%%:*}" || status=1
          done
          exit "$status"

      - name: Merge the release date
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.publish_needed == 'true'
        env:
          FINISH: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.finish }}
          RELEASE_APPROVER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.approver-token }}
          RELEASE_REVIEWER_TEAM: ${{ inputs.reviewer-team }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          # One version failing must not hold back the versions after it.
          status=0
          for release in $FINISH; do
            bash "$RELEASE_SCRIPTS/bash/merge_plugin_release_date_pr.sh" "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "${release%%:*}" || status=1
          done
          exit "$status"

      # Last, so the versions being finished are not held back with the new one.
      - name: Fail when CI held the release back
        if: always() && steps.prepare.outputs.ci_held != ''
        env:
          CI_HELD: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.ci_held }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::error::$CI_HELD"
          exit 1

name: PHPStan check

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plugin-name:
        description: "Name of the plugin, e.g. LoginLdap"
        required: true
        type: string
      dependent-plugins:
        description: "Space-separated repository slugs to check out, e.g. 'innocraft/plugin-Funnels'"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      php-version:
        description: "PHP version the job runs on; the analysis level and phpVersion come from the plugin's phpstan.neon. Accepts a literal version or one of the shared aliases (matomo5_min_php, matomo5_max_php, matomo6_min_php, matomo6_max_php), which track a Matomo major's floor and ceiling centrally. The default clears Matomo 6's floor of 8.1: a plugin declaring >=6.0.0-b1 resolves both legs to 6.x-dev until 6.0.0 is tagged, and matomo5_min_php (7.2) cannot bootstrap it."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'matomo6_min_php'
      scripts-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/github-action-tests to take the helper scripts from. Pinning the workflow does not pin these: pass a SHA from that repository, which is a different repository with different SHAs."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows to take the PHPStan bootstrap from. This is this repository, so the workflow SHA is the right value when pinning."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      matomo-targets:
        description: >-
          JSON array of {target, php} objects, one per analysis run. Analysing the minimum target
          is what catches a plugin calling a core API that does not exist yet in the oldest Matomo
          its plugin.json supports. `php` is optional and falls back to the php-version input; set
          it per target when the targets span Matomo majors, because a Matomo 6 checkout cannot be
          bootstrapped by the PHP 7.2 that Matomo 5 allows.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '[{"target": "minimum_required_matomo"}, {"target": "maximum_supported_matomo"}]'
    secrets:
      TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN:
        required: false

# The job only reads the two repositories; everything else stays at none so any
# caller with default workflow permissions can use this without granting scopes.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  phpstan:
    name: PHPStan (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.matomo-targets) }}
    env:
      PLUGIN_NAME: ${{ inputs.plugin-name }}
      DEPENDENT_PLUGINS: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins }}
      # Unique so they cannot collide with a directory the caller tracks, and
      # dot-prefixed so checkout_matomo.sh's `cp -R !($PLUGIN_NAME)` leaves them
      # out of the plugin it assembles: that glob enables extglob, not dotglob.
      HELPERS_DIR: .github-action-tests-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      WORKFLOWS_DIR: .plugin-ci-workflows-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    steps:
      - name: Validate inputs
        run: |
          if [[ ! "$PLUGIN_NAME" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]]; then
            echo "Invalid plugin-name: $PLUGIN_NAME"
            exit 1
          fi

          # checkout_dependent_plugins.sh does `rm -rf plugins/<derived-name>` before
          # cloning, so a dependent plugin resolving to the plugin under test would
          # silently replace it and analyse the wrong code. Refuse instead.
          for slug in $DEPENDENT_PLUGINS; do
            name=${slug##*/}
            name=${name#plugin-}
            if [[ "$name" == "$PLUGIN_NAME" ]]; then
              echo "dependent-plugins entry '$slug' resolves to the plugin under test ($PLUGIN_NAME)."
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          lfs: false
          persist-credentials: false

      # No GitHub context identifies the called workflow's own commit (verified
      # empirically: github.job_workflow_sha evaluates to empty), so pinning the
      # scripts is the caller's job via scripts-ref. This runs before PHP is set up
      # because the version aliases are resolved by one of those scripts.
      - name: Check out github-action-tests repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/github-action-tests
          ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.HELPERS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # A reusable workflow does not bring its own repository into the caller's
      # workspace, so the PHPStan bootstrap this workflow ships alongside it needs
      # checking out explicitly too.
      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: ${{ env.WORKFLOWS_DIR }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve PHP version
        id: resolve-php
        shell: bash
        env:
          # per-target when the targets span Matomo majors, else the workflow-wide input
          PHP_VERSION_INPUT: ${{ matrix.php || inputs.php-version }}
        run: |
          RESOLVED_VERSION=$("$HELPERS_DIR/scripts/bash/resolve_php_version.sh" "$PHP_VERSION_INPUT")

          echo "Resolved php-version '$PHP_VERSION_INPUT' to '$RESOLVED_VERSION'"
          echo "version=$RESOLVED_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Setup PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ steps.resolve-php.outputs.version }}

      - name: checkout matomo for plugin builds
        shell: bash
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ env.HELPERS_DIR }}/scripts/bash/checkout_matomo.sh
        env:
          WORKSPACE: ${{ github.workspace }}
          ACTION_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ env.HELPERS_DIR }}
          MATOMO_TEST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}

      # Belt and braces: the dot prefix already keeps the helper checkouts out of
      # `cp -R !($PLUGIN_NAME)`, but that depends on dotglob staying off in a script
      # this repository does not own. The names are run-scoped, so this can only ever
      # remove our own copies.
      - name: Remove any helper checkout copied into the plugin
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd "${{ github.workspace }}/matomo/plugins/$PLUGIN_NAME"
          rm -rf "$HELPERS_DIR" "$WORKFLOWS_DIR"

      - name: Check the PHP version can bootstrap this Matomo
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        env:
          MATOMO_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          # bootstrap-phpstan.php executes core rather than only parsing it, so analysing a
          # Matomo 6 checkout under the PHP 7.2 that Matomo 5 allows dies on 8.1 syntax partway
          # through. Catch it here, where the message can say what to change.
          # `|| true`: GitHub runs `run:` with `-e -o pipefail`, so without it a non-matching
          # grep exits the step and the guard below is unreachable dead code.
          MATOMO_MIN_PHP=$(grep -oE "piwik_minimumPHPVersion = '[0-9.]+'" core/testMinimumPhpVersion.php 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "[0-9]+\.[0-9.]+" | head -1 || true)

          if [ -z "$MATOMO_MIN_PHP" ]; then
            echo "Could not read piwik_minimumPHPVersion; skipping the compatibility check."
            exit 0
          fi

          # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # $argv is PHP's, and must not be expanded by the shell
          if ! php -r 'exit(version_compare(PHP_VERSION, $argv[1], ">=") ? 0 : 1);' "$MATOMO_MIN_PHP"; then
            echo "::error::Matomo target '$MATOMO_TARGET' requires PHP >= $MATOMO_MIN_PHP but this job runs $(php -r 'echo PHP_VERSION;'). Give this target its own PHP in the matomo-targets input, for example {\"target\": \"$MATOMO_TARGET\", \"php\": \"matomo6_min_php\"}."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "PHP $(php -r 'echo PHP_VERSION;') satisfies this Matomo's floor of $MATOMO_MIN_PHP."

      - name: Provide the PHPStan bootstrap when Matomo predates it
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        run: |
          if [ -f bootstrap-phpstan.php ]; then
            echo "Matomo provides bootstrap-phpstan.php."
            exit 0
          fi
          # Matomo only ships this file from 5.4.0, and plugin phpstan.neon files reference it
          # as ../../bootstrap-phpstan.php, so without it PHPStan exits before analysing
          # anything on older targets. It has to be copied into the Matomo root rather than
          # referenced in place: it derives PIWIK_DOCUMENT_ROOT from its own location.
          cp "${{ github.workspace }}/$WORKFLOWS_DIR/artifacts/bootstrap-phpstan.php" bootstrap-phpstan.php
          echo "Matomo predates bootstrap-phpstan.php; using the copy from plugin-ci-workflows."

      - name: prepare setup
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
          echo -e "composer install"
          composer install --ignore-platform-reqs

      - name: Provide PHPStan itself when Matomo predates it
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        run: |
          if [ -x vendor/bin/phpstan ]; then
            echo "Matomo provides PHPStan."
            exit 0
          fi
          # Matomo gained phpstan/phpstan, the composer `phpstan` script and
          # bootstrap-phpstan.php in one commit, released in 5.4.0. On an older target there
          # is no analyser at all, so install the same constraint that Matomo declares rather
          # than the newest release, whose own findings would differ from the max leg's.
          # The range is deliberately not pinned to an exact version: it mirrors what Matomo
          # itself resolves, and pinning here would drift from the analyser the max leg uses.
          echo "Matomo predates phpstan/phpstan; installing ~1.12 to analyse against it."
          composer require --dev --ignore-platform-reqs --no-interaction "phpstan/phpstan:~1.12"

      - name: checkout additional plugins
        if: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins != '' }}
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ env.HELPERS_DIR }}/scripts/bash/checkout_dependent_plugins.sh
        env:
          GITHUB_USER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN || github.token }}
          TARGET_BRANCH: ${{ github.base_ref || github.ref_name }}

      # checkout_dependent_plugins.sh prints "Failed to checkout ... Skipping." and still exits 0,
      # so a caller that forgets `secrets: inherit`, or a repository without TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN,
      # falls back to github.token, cannot clone innocraft/*, and PHPStan then analyses a tree
      # missing a dependency -- reported as a wall of unrelated errors rather than a setup fault.
      - name: Check every dependent plugin was actually checked out
        if: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins != '' }}
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        run: |
          MISSING=""
          for slug in $DEPENDENT_PLUGINS; do
            name=${slug##*/}
            name=${name#plugin-}
            [ -d "plugins/$name" ] || MISSING="$MISSING $slug"
          done

          if [ -n "$MISSING" ]; then
            echo "::error::These dependent plugins were not checked out:$MISSING. The most likely cause is a missing or unscoped TESTS_ACCESS_TOKEN, which makes the clone fall back to a token that cannot read private repositories."
            exit 1
          fi

      # The helper clones over https://$TOKEN:[REDACTED], and git keeps that URL
      # in .git/config. PHPStan then runs the plugin's own phpstan.neon, which can
      # execute PHP through bootstrapFiles, so the token must not still be on disk.
      # Nothing downstream needs plugin git metadata.
      - name: Scrub credentials from the checked out plugins
        if: ${{ inputs.dependent-plugins != '' }}
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        run: |
          find plugins -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name .git -exec rm -rf {} +
          if grep -rIl "x-access-token\|@github.com" plugins --include=config 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::Credential material still present under plugins/ after scrubbing."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: "Restore result cache"
        uses: actions/cache/restore@caa296126883cff596d87d8935842f9db880ef25 # v5.1.0
        with:
          path: /tmp/phpstan # same as in phpstan.neon
          # the target is part of the key because the legs analyse different Matomo trees and
          # both save within one run, which would otherwise collide on a single key
          key: "phpstan-result-cache-${{ matrix.target }}-${{ github.run_id }}"
          restore-keys: |
            phpstan-result-cache-${{ matrix.target }}-

      - name: PHPStan whole repo
        id: phpstan-all
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/matomo
        env:
          MATOMO_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        # not `composer run phpstan`: that script arrived with PHPStan itself in 5.4.0, so it
        # does not exist on older targets. The binary is equivalent — the script is only
        # `phpstan analyse -c phpstan.neon`, whose config this command overrides anyway.
        run: |
          CONFIG="plugins/${PLUGIN_NAME}/phpstan.neon"

          # A plugin may guard a newer core API behind class_exists and still be analysed
          # against an older Matomo that lacks it, which PHPStan cannot see through. An
          # optional phpstan-min-matomo.neon holds those ignores. It applies to this leg only:
          # on the maximum leg the error does not occur, so the same ignore would be unmatched
          # and reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors would fail that leg instead.
          if [ "$MATOMO_TARGET" = 'minimum_required_matomo' ] \
            && [ -f "plugins/${PLUGIN_NAME}/phpstan-min-matomo.neon" ]; then
            CONFIG="plugins/${PLUGIN_NAME}/phpstan-min-matomo.neon"
            echo "Using the plugin's minimum-target config: $CONFIG"
          fi

          vendor/bin/phpstan analyse -vvv -c "$CONFIG"

      # Only a clean run's cache is worth keeping: the plugin's own phpstan.neon executes in this
      # job, so a cache written by a failed analysis is both useless and attacker-influenced.
      - name: "Save result cache"
        uses: actions/cache/save@caa296126883cff596d87d8935842f9db880ef25 # v5.1.0
        if: ${{ success() }}
        with:
          path: /tmp/phpstan # same as in phpstan.neon
          key: "phpstan-result-cache-${{ matrix.target }}-${{ github.run_id }}"

# Updates a plugin's scoped dependencies and opens (or refreshes) a pull request with the result.
#
# Dependabot cannot do this for a plugin that commits only vendor/prefixed. It edits composer.json
# and composer.lock and nothing else, so its pull request would test the old prefixed code under a
# new lock file and pass. The tree has to be rebuilt the way a developer rebuilds it locally:
# composer update, then matomo-scoper, then Rector. The last two are the scope-dependencies action
# in this repository, which runs scripts/bash/scope_plugin_dependencies.sh and needs neither Matomo
# core nor DevPluginCommands.
#
# The caller keeps the `schedule` trigger, because a reusable workflow's own cron would fire in this
# repository rather than the plugin's.

name: Vendored dependencies update

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      branch:
        description: "Branch to update and to open the pull request against. Defaults to the ref the caller ran on, which for a schedule is the default branch."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      php-version:
        description: "PHP to run composer, matomo-scoper and Rector on, 8.1 or later. This is not the plugin's floor: dependencies resolve against config.platform.php in the plugin's composer.json, or platform-php when it has none."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '8.3'
      platform-php:
        description: "PHP version to resolve dependencies against when the plugin's composer.json has no config.platform.php, usually the plugin's minimum, such as 8.1.0. It is set only for the update, so neither composer.json nor composer.lock keeps it. A config.platform.php in composer.json takes precedence."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      downgrade-php:
        description: "PHP version to transpile vendor/prefixed down to with Rector: 'auto' reads it from plugin.json and the composer platform, 'none' skips Rector, or pass 7.3 or 8.1."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'auto'
      allowed-unprefixed-namespaces:
        description: "Whitespace-separated namespaces allowed to remain outside Matomo\\Dependencies\\<plugin> in vendor/prefixed, besides Composer\\Autoload, which is always allowed."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      scoper-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/matomo-scoper. Empty uses the commit scripts/bash/scope_plugin_dependencies.sh pins."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      workflows-ref:
        description: "Ref of this repository to take the scope-dependencies action and the plugin floor resolver from."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      scripts-ref:
        description: "Ref of matomo-org/github-action-tests to take the PHP version alias table from, used to compare the platform PHP with the plugin's minimum. That is a different repository with different SHAs."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'main'
      bump-version:
        description: "Record the update in plugin.json and CHANGELOG.md: bump a released version to its next patch with a new changelog entry, or add to the entry of a version not yet released. The entry is left undated."
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true
      changelog-entry:
        description: "The changelog line bump-version adds."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Updated dependencies'
      reviewer-team:
        description: "Slug of the team in the repository's organisation whose review the pull request requests while nobody is requested and nobody has reviewed. Empty picks plugin-reviewers in matomo-org and premium-plugins-reviewers in innocraft."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
    secrets:
      DEPS_PR_TOKEN:
        [REDACTED] >-
          Pushes the update branch and opens the pull request. Optional, but without it the
          pull request is opened with GITHUB_TOKEN, which needs the repository or organisation
          setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests", off by default.
          GitHub also starts no workflow runs for events that token causes -- so the plugin's CI
          does not run on the pull request by itself. After each refresh, close and reopen it to
          run Plugins CI, and run matomo-tests.yml on the update branch from the Actions tab: the
          matomo-tests.yml that `generate:test-action` writes does not subscribe to `reopened`.
          Pushing to it starts both, but stops this workflow refreshing it. It also requests the
          team review, so a token that cannot request one fails the run; a GitHub App needs
          organisation Members read access for that. Without the token no review is requested.
        required: false

# The job that runs composer update can also run code the newly resolved packages ship, such as a
# Composer plugin, so it gets no write access. Only the pull-request job holds a write token, and
# it runs nothing from the dependencies.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Named without ${{ github.workflow }}: in a reusable workflow that resolves to the CALLER's
# workflow name, which collides with a caller group of the same name.
concurrency:
  group: plugin-vendored-deps-update-${{ inputs.branch || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  BASE_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch || github.ref_name }}
  PLUGIN_DIR: plugin
  UPDATE_BRANCH: automated/vendored-dependencies-${{ inputs.branch || github.ref_name }}
  BOT_EMAIL: 41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com

jobs:
  update:
    name: Update scoped dependencies
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # 30 for the update itself, and 15 for find_new_floor_php_gaps.sh, whose two PHPStan runs may take 5 each.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read # the human-commit check lists open pull requests
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed }}
      base-sha: ${{ steps.update.outputs.base-sha }}
      update-head: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.head }}
      artifact: ${{ steps.update.outputs.artifact }}
      bump-sha256: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.sha256 }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out the plugin
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.BASE_BRANCH }}
          path: ${{ env.PLUGIN_DIR }}
          lfs: false
          persist-credentials: false

      # Checked out rather than referenced as matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows/actions/...@ref, because
      # a `uses:` ref cannot come from an input, and workflows-ref has to reach the action too.
      - name: Check out plugin-ci-workflows repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/plugin-ci-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          path: .plugin-ci-workflows
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ inputs.php-version }}
          coverage: none
          tools: composer:v2

      # Composer resolves against the PHP it runs on, not require.php, so without a platform PHP a run
      # on the tooling PHP above would lock packages the plugin's own floor cannot install.
      - name: Resolve the platform PHP
        id: platform
        shell: bash
        env:
          PHP_VERSION: ${{ inputs.php-version }}
          PLATFORM_INPUT: ${{ inputs.platform-php }}
        run: |
          # A line break, or a carriage return, could start a workflow command of its own in what
          # is echoed.
          pin=$(jq -r '.config.platform.php // empty | tostring | gsub("[\r\n]"; " ")' "$PLUGIN_DIR/composer.json")
          shown=${PLATFORM_INPUT//[$'\r\n']/ }
          # 8.1 and 8.1.0 are the same platform.
          patch_level() { if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then echo "$1.0"; else echo "$1"; fi; }
          if [ -n "$pin" ]; then
            echo "Resolving against platform PHP $pin, from composer.json."
            if [ -n "$PLATFORM_INPUT" ] && [ "$(patch_level "$PLATFORM_INPUT")" != "$(patch_level "$pin")" ]; then
              echo "::warning file=composer.json::Ignoring platform-php $shown, because composer.json pins $pin."
            fi
            echo "platform=$pin" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ -n "$PLATFORM_INPUT" ]; then
            if ! [[ "$PLATFORM_INPUT" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::platform-php must be a PHP version such as 8.1.0, not '$shown'."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Resolving against platform PHP $PLATFORM_INPUT, from the platform-php input."
            echo "temporary=$PLATFORM_INPUT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "platform=$PLATFORM_INPUT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::error file=composer.json::composer.json has no config.platform.php and no platform-php was passed, so dependencies would resolve against PHP $PHP_VERSION rather than the plugin's minimum. Pass platform-php, or pin it in composer.json."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Refreshing the branch force-pushes it, so anything a person added since -- a changelog entry,
      # a version bump, a fix to the scoped tree -- would be lost. Leave such a branch alone.
      - name: Check the update branch has no human commits
        id: branch
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # Only a 404 means there is no branch yet. Reading any failure as absence would let a rate
          # limit or an outage wave the force-push through.
          if ! head=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/branches/$UPDATE_BRANCH" --jq .commit.sha 2>&1); then
            case "$head" in
              *"HTTP 404"*)
                echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                exit 0
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::error::Could not check whether $UPDATE_BRANCH exists: $head"
            exit 1
          fi
          # The pull-request job pushes minutes later, and checks the branch is still here.
          echo "head=$head" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Only an open pull request's work needs keeping. A squash-merge leaves the branch behind
          # with its human commits still unmerged by ancestry, and without this every later run would
          # skip until someone deleted the branch.
          if ! open=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls?head=${GITHUB_REPOSITORY%%/*}:$UPDATE_BRANCH&state=open" --jq length); then
            echo "::error::Could not list the pull requests from $UPDATE_BRANCH."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$open" = "0" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          if ! others=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/compare/$BASE_BRANCH...$UPDATE_BRANCH" \
            --jq "[.commits[] | select(.commit.author.email != \"$BOT_EMAIL\" or .commit.committer.email != \"$BOT_EMAIL\")] | length"); then
            echo "::error::Could not list the commits on $UPDATE_BRANCH."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$others" != "0" ]; then
            echo "::notice::$UPDATE_BRANCH carries $others commit(s) not made by this workflow, so its open pull request was left as it is. Merge or close the pull request to get a fresh update."
            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # Only the comparison below reads this checkout, and that step only warns, so a scripts-ref that
      # cannot be fetched must not stop the update either.
      - name: Check out github-action-tests repository
        id: action-tests
        if: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.skip != 'true' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: matomo-org/github-action-tests
          ref: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          path: .github-action-tests
          persist-credentials: false

      # Matomo lets a plugin activate on the PHP its plugin.json declares, so a platform above that
      # can lock packages that fail for some of its users. This only warns: closing the gap means
      # changing the plugin, and failing would hold back every update until someone did.
      - name: Compare the platform PHP with the plugin's minimum
        if: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.skip != 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          PLATFORM: ${{ steps.platform.outputs.platform }}
          TEMPORARY_PLATFORM: ${{ steps.platform.outputs.temporary }}
          WORKFLOWS_REF: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          SCRIPTS_REF: ${{ inputs.scripts-ref }}
          SCRIPTS_CHECKOUT: ${{ steps.action-tests.outcome }}
          RESOLVER: .plugin-ci-workflows/scripts/bash/resolve_plugin_min_php.sh
          ALIAS_RESOLVER: .github-action-tests/scripts/bash/resolve_php_version.sh
        run: |
          # % first: GitHub unescapes %25 too, so a literal %0A in a value would otherwise come back
          # out as a real newline.
          escape() { local s=${1//%/%25}; printf '%s' "${s//[$'\r\n']/ }"; }
          # Scheduled runs' annotations go unread, so whoever merges the update sees the result in the
          # pull request body too.
          to_body() { printf '> [!%s]\n> %s\n' "$1" "${2//[$'\r\n']/ }" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/platform-check.md"; }
          skip() {
            local reason="Could not compare platform PHP $PLATFORM with the plugin's minimum: $1"
            echo "::warning::$(escape "$reason")"
            to_body NOTE "$reason"
            exit 0
          }
          [ -f "$RESOLVER" ] || skip "workflows-ref '$WORKFLOWS_REF' does not carry scripts/bash/resolve_plugin_min_php.sh."
          [ "$SCRIPTS_CHECKOUT" = success ] || skip "scripts-ref '$SCRIPTS_REF' could not be checked out."
          [ -f "$ALIAS_RESOLVER" ] || skip "scripts-ref '$SCRIPTS_REF' does not carry scripts/bash/resolve_php_version.sh."
          [[ "$PLATFORM" =~ ^([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+) ]] || skip "the platform is not a PHP version."
          platform_major=${BASH_REMATCH[1]} platform_minor=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}

          [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.json" ] || skip "the plugin has no plugin.json."
          # The resolver also counts config.platform.php as a floor, which would compare the pin with
          # itself, so it sees plugin.json alone.
          manifest=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$manifest"' EXIT
          cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.json" "$manifest/"
          declared=$(bash "$RESOLVER" "$manifest" 2>"$manifest/notes") || skip "$(tail -n 1 "$manifest/notes" | sed "s#$manifest#$PLUGIN_DIR#g") This comparison reads plugin.json alone."
          # The resolver answers with an alias such as matomo6_min_php when plugin.json declares no PHP.
          if [[ "$declared" == matomo* ]]; then
            source="plugin.json's Matomo requirement" remedy='set a minimum in plugin.json require.php'
          else
            source='plugin.json require.php' remedy='raise require.php in plugin.json'
          fi
          floor=$(bash "$ALIAS_RESOLVER" "$declared") || skip "the alias table at scripts-ref '$SCRIPTS_REF' could not resolve '$declared'."
          [[ "$floor" =~ ^([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)$ ]] || skip "'$floor' is not a PHP version the alias table knows."
          floor_major=${BASH_REMATCH[1]} floor_minor=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}

          # 10#, or bash reads a zero-padded 08 as a malformed octal number.
          if (( 10#$platform_major > 10#$floor_major || (10#$platform_major == 10#$floor_major && 10#$platform_minor > 10#$floor_minor) )); then
            if [ -n "$TEMPORARY_PLATFORM" ]; then setting='the platform-php input'; else setting='config.platform.php in composer.json'; fi
            gap="Dependencies resolve against PHP $PLATFORM, but $source lets the plugin run on PHP $floor, so this update can lock packages that fail there. Set $setting to the lowest PHP $floor release $source allows, or $remedy if the plugin needs PHP $PLATFORM."
            echo "::warning file=plugin.json::$(escape "$gap")"
            to_body WARNING "$gap"
          else
            result="Platform PHP $PLATFORM is not above the plugin's minimum, PHP $floor from $source."
            printf '%s\n' "${result//[$'\r\n']/ }"
          fi

      # Before the update, so no dependency code has run yet: the pull-request job trusts this step's
      # outputs, and checks the bumped files against the hash among them. Never fails the run: a
      # version left alone is something a person can add, and an update held back is not.
      - name: Bump the plugin version
        id: bump
        if: ${{ inputs.bump-version && steps.branch.outputs.skip != 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ENTRY: ${{ inputs.changelog-entry }}
          WORKFLOWS_REF: ${{ inputs.workflows-ref }}
          BUMP: .plugin-ci-workflows/scripts/python/bump_plugin_version.py
        run: |
          # On copies, so the rebuild and the checks after it see the plugin as committed.
          work="$RUNNER_TEMP/bump"
          rm -rf "$work"
          mkdir -p "$work"
          for file in plugin.json CHANGELOG.md; do
            if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/$file" ] && [ ! -L "$PLUGIN_DIR/$file" ]; then
              cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/$file" "$work/"
            fi
          done
          # A version is released once it is tagged. A changelog date says nothing either way: plenty
          # of released versions have none.
          version=$(jq -r '.version // empty' "$work/plugin.json" 2>/dev/null) || version=''
          released=unreleased
          note=''
          unchecked="The version was not bumped, because whether $version is released could not be checked."
          if [ ! -f "$BUMP" ]; then
            note="The version was not bumped, because workflows-ref '$WORKFLOWS_REF' does not have scripts/python/bump_plugin_version.py."
          elif [ -z "${ENTRY//[[:space:]]/}" ]; then
            note="The version was not bumped, because the changelog-entry input is empty."
          elif ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9A-Za-z.+-]+$ ]]; then
            note="The version was not bumped, because plugin.json has no version to look up."
          else
            for tag in "$version" "v$version"; do
              if out=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/ref/tags/$tag" --jq .ref 2>&1); then
                released=released
                break
              fi
              case "$out" in
                *"HTTP 404"*) ;;
                *)
                  echo "::warning::Could not look up tag $tag: ${out//[$'\r\n']/ }"
                  note="$unchecked"
                  break
                  ;;
              esac
            done
            # A plugin.json behind its tags would otherwise be bumped to a version already released.
            if [ -z "$note" ] && [[ "$version" =~ ^([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)$ ]]; then
              next="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}.${BASH_REMATCH[2]}.$((10#${BASH_REMATCH[3]} + 1))"
              for tag in "$next" "v$next"; do
                if out=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/ref/tags/$tag" --jq .ref 2>&1); then
                  note="The version was not bumped, because $next is already tagged while plugin.json says $version."
                  break
                fi
                case "$out" in
                  *"HTTP 404"*) ;;
                  *)
                    echo "::warning::Could not look up tag $tag: ${out//[$'\r\n']/ }"
                    note="The version was not bumped, because whether $next is already released could not be checked."
                    break
                    ;;
                esac
              done
            fi
            # With no tags at all, an untagged version says nothing about whether it was released.
            if [ -z "$note" ] && [ "$released" = unreleased ]; then
              if ! count=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/tags?per_page=1" --jq length 2>&1); then
                echo "::warning::Could not list the repository's tags: ${count//[$'\r\n']/ }"
                note="$unchecked"
              elif [ "$count" = 0 ]; then
                note="$unchecked The repository has no tags."
              fi
            fi
          fi
          if [ -z "$note" ]; then
            status=0
            # The script comes from the caller's workflows-ref, so it gets no token.
            note=$(env -u GH_TOKEN python3 -I "$BUMP" "$work" "$released" "$ENTRY") || status=$?
            if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ "$status" -ne 3 ]; then
              echo "::warning::bump_plugin_version.py exited $status."
              note="The version was not bumped, because the script that bumps it failed; the run's log says why."
            elif [ "$status" -eq 0 ] && ! { cmp -s "$work/plugin.json" "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.json" \
              && cmp -s "$work/CHANGELOG.md" "$PLUGIN_DIR/CHANGELOG.md"; }; then
              echo "sha256=$(cd "$work" && sha256sum plugin.json CHANGELOG.md | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            fi
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$note"
          if [[ "$note" == "The version was not bumped"* ]]; then
            note+=" This changes code the plugin ships, so it needs the usual changelog entry and version bump before release."
          fi
          # On one line, so it cannot add an output of its own.
          echo "note=${note//[$'\r\n']/ }" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # A full update also runs post-update-cmd, which is where plugins trim
      # google/apiclient-services with Google\Task\Composer::cleanup.
      - name: Update dependencies
        id: update
        if: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.skip != 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          TEMPORARY_PLATFORM: ${{ steps.platform.outputs.temporary }}
        run: |
          log=$(mktemp)
          # Before composer, whose plugins run with this checkout writable and could move HEAD to a
          # commit the pull-request job would then check out.
          base=$(git -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" rev-parse HEAD)
          if [ -n "$TEMPORARY_PLATFORM" ]; then
            cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/composer.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/composer.json"
            composer config --working-dir="$PLUGIN_DIR" platform.php "$TEMPORARY_PLATFORM"
          fi
          composer update --working-dir="$PLUGIN_DIR" --no-interaction --no-progress 2>&1 | tee "$log"
          if [ -n "$TEMPORARY_PLATFORM" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/composer.json" "$PLUGIN_DIR/composer.json"
            # The lock's content hash covers config.platform, and the lock records it as
            # platform-overrides. --lock rewrites both from the restored composer.json, and keeps
            # every package at its locked version and reference. It still checks them against the
            # runner's PHP, though, which can sit on either side of the platform: a package capped
            # at ^7.2 || ~8.0.0 fails on a newer runner, one needing 8.4 on an older one. php* also
            # covers php-64bit and the like, which the platform sets too. Nothing is re-resolved, so
            # ignoring them cannot change what is locked.
            composer update --lock --no-install --ignore-platform-req='php*' --no-scripts --working-dir="$PLUGIN_DIR" --no-interaction --no-progress
          fi

          # The same comparison as check_scoped_tree.sh, which fails a run whose tree did not follow it.
          lock_packages() {
            jq -S '[(.packages // [])[] | {name, version, source: .source.reference, dist: (.dist.reference // .dist.url)}]'
          }
          if cmp -s <(git -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" show "$base:./composer.lock" | lock_packages) <(lock_packages < "$PLUGIN_DIR/composer.lock"); then
            echo "::notice::Every dependency is already at the newest version composer.json allows."
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          {
            echo "changed=true"
            echo "base-sha=$base"
            # One run holds every branch of a matrix caller, and an artifact name is unique per run.
            # The hash keeps a/b and a-b apart once the slash is replaced.
            echo "artifact=rebuilt-tree-${BASE_BRANCH//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/-}-$(printf '%s' "$BASE_BRANCH" | sha256sum | cut -c1-8)"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Only the lock file operations: after "Installing dependencies from lock file" composer
          # lists every package it extracts, which is the whole tree for an unprefixed vendor/ that
          # is never committed.
          sed -n '/^Lock file operations/,/^Installing dependencies from lock file/p' "$log" \
            | { grep -E '^  - (Upgrading|Downgrading|Locking|Removing)' || true; } \
            | sed -E 's/^  - /- /' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/package-changes.md"
          if [ ! -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/package-changes.md" ]; then
            echo "Composer listed no package operations; the \`composer.lock\` diff shows what changed." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/package-changes.md"
          fi
          rm -f "$log"

      - name: Scope, downgrade and check
        id: scope
        if: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true' }}
        uses: ./.plugin-ci-workflows/actions/scope-dependencies
        with:
          plugin-path: ${{ env.PLUGIN_DIR }}
          downgrade-php: ${{ inputs.downgrade-php }}
          allowed-unprefixed-namespaces: ${{ inputs.allowed-unprefixed-namespaces }}
          scoper-ref: ${{ inputs.scoper-ref }}

      # For the class-load check and find_new_floor_php_gaps.sh, which have to run on the floor: a class
      # can load on a newer PHP only, and PHPStan counts whatever the running PHP has as present. Nothing
      # after the checks in this job runs PHP. A failed setup skips them rather than the pull request;
      # running them on the runner's PHP instead would report nothing, falsely.
      - name: Choose the floor PHP
        id: floor-version
        if: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true' && steps.scope.outputs.downgrade-php-version != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          DOWNGRADE: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.downgrade-php-version }}
        run: |
          # PHPStan needs 7.4, so it checks a 7.3 floor on that. The classes are loaded on the floor itself.
          php="$DOWNGRADE"
          [ "$DOWNGRADE" != 7.3 ] || php=7.4
          echo "php=$php" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "load=$DOWNGRADE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Setup the PHP the classes load on
        id: load-php
        if: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true' && steps.scope.outputs.downgrade-php-version != '' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ steps.floor-version.outputs.load }}
          coverage: none
          tools: none

      # Fails rather than warns: a class that loaded before the rebuild and no longer does is a fatal
      # error for whatever touches it. A check that cannot run only warns, and the body says so.
      - name: Check the rebuilt classes load on the floor PHP
        id: load-check
        if: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true' && steps.scope.outputs.downgrade-php-version != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
